summary: Browning and Sawin develop a geometric version of the Hardy–Littlewood circle method over F_q(T), with ℓ-adic analogues of the major and minor arcs, to control the compactly supported cohomology of spaces of rational curves on smooth hypersurfaces of low degree. They deduce that these spaces are irreducible of the expected dimension, and compare their Betti numbers with those of spaces of maps into the complex hypersurface. Complete (cc-442dc5): every numbered statement is an item, every missing item is routed exactly once, and twenty-eight findings are recorded. The minor-arc bound behind Proposition 2.6 and its corollaries needs a repaired range (E1–E3), and Lemma 7.2 is false with the compact-open topology (E28). Not formalised. After the review (REV-PAPER-BROWNING-SAWIN-20) there are 149 items (11 library, 11 planned, 127 missing) and 46 source issues; every locator now gives the published version. The review confirmed the extraction's corrections and repairs, including its topology analysis showing that Lemma 7.2 fails for the compact-open reading of the germ space (so Conjecture 7.1 also fails there at j = 1).

conventions.geometry: K a field; n≥2, k≥3; f∈K[x1,…,xn] has degree k, X={f=0} smooth affine, and its leading form f0 defines a smooth projective hypersurface Z⊂P^{n−1}. Fix a NONZERO vector x∈K^n with f0(x)=0, representing P∈Z. A chosen representative, not only the projective class, fixes the leading coefficients.
conventions.ranges: D=d(n−k), L=kd, K0=k−1, t=floor(d/K0), δ=n/2^k−k+1. Main range d≥K0≥2 and δ>0. Integer cohomological indices; thresholds are rational strict inequalities. Acyclic cohomological degree and dimension of an empty differencing locus are −∞, with extended arithmetic.
conventions.coefficients: Étale cohomology is geometric compact-support cohomology unless explicitly ordinary. In characteristic p assume p>k; choose ℓ≠p of even multiplicative order modulo p when using sign-conjugacy/minor arcs. Rank-one Artin–Schreier sheaves use E=Q_ℓ(μ_p); retain the coefficient-extension/descent debt before asserting all constructions over Q_ℓ. Frobenius convention gives E(−a) eigenvalue q^a. In characteristic zero spread out the full pair (f,x), not f alone.
conventions.derived: Cohomological shift: H^i(C[a])=H^{i+a}(C). Thus RΓ_c(A^r,E)=E[−2r](−r). Reduced compact cohomology means the homotopy fibre of the trace, not unreduced cohomology with an informal top-degree deletion. S_m acts with Koszul signs on derived tensor powers.
conventions.planning: All APIs, tests, modules, dependencies and proofs below are plans. No Lean file or Lean compilation is supplied. The corrected conservative range is a mathematical deduction from the paper's intermediate bounds, not an independently formalised proof. Original sharp claims are retained as explicitly gated targets, never silently certified.

items.name: Polynomial mapping scheme with a fixed leading vector
items.statement: Mor_{d,x} represents g_j=x_j T^d+Σ_{i<d}a_{i,j}T^i with f(g_1,…,g_n)=0. It is an affine scheme in nd coefficients cut out by the kd non-leading coefficients; f0(x)=0 kills degree kd. Individual g_j have degree ≤d; their joint degree is d. No quotient by reparametrization is taken.
unitTests: x_j=0 allows deg(g_j)<d
g↦g(aT+b) changes the fixed leading vector by a^d

items.name: Expected dimension lower bound
items.statement: Every nonempty irreducible component of Mor_{d,x} over an algebraic closure has dimension at least nd−kd=D, since there are kd defining equations.
items.locator: §1, p.893 (expected dimension); §2, proof of Corollary 2.9, p.907 (arXiv v3: p.1; p.14)

items.name: Ordered and unordered configurations of the affine line
items.statement: PConf_m={ (a_1,…,a_m)∈A^m : a_i≠a_j for i≠j }; its S_m quotient is Conf_m, the open space of squarefree monic degree-m polynomials. The quotient map is a finite étale S_m-torsor, including m=0 as a point.
items.locator: §1, p.894; §3, proof of Lemma 3.9, p.919 (arXiv v3: p.2; p.24)
unitTests: PConf_0=Spec K, PConf_1=A1
char K dividing m! does not prevent the constant S_m torsor from being étale

items.name: Middle compact cohomology and parity-twisted tensors
items.statement: V=H_c^{n−1}(X,E); define W_m=(RΓ_c(PConf_m,E)⊗V^{⊗m}⊗sgn^{n−1})^{S_m}. The sign factor comes from placing each V in cohomological degree n−1.
items.locator: §1, Theorem 1.1, p.894; §3, Corollary 3.12 and its proof, p.920 (arXiv v3: p.2; p.26)
unitTests: m=0 gives E in degree 0
transposition gives a minus sign exactly when n−1 is odd

items.name: Residue-coefficient phase
items.statement: For a∈A^{dn}, b∈A^L set e(a,b)=[T^{−1}](Σ_{r=1}^L b_rT^{−r})f(g_1(T),…,g_n(T)). This is a polynomial map A^{dn}×A^L→A1, linear in b and of degree ≤k in a.
unitTests: b=0 gives 0
adding a constant c to f changes e by c*b1

items.name: Artin–Schreier rank-one coefficient sheaf
items.statement: For a non-trivial additive character ψ: F_q → E^× (E ⊇ μ_p, char E = 0), L_ψ is the lisse rank-one E-sheaf on A^1_{F_q} obtained from the F_q-torsor u^q − u = x through ψ (equivalently L_ψ = [x↦ax]^*L_{ψ0∘Tr} when ψ(x) = ψ0(Tr_{F_q/F_p}(ax)) with ψ0 a character of F_p, L_{ψ0} being the ψ0-isotypic part of the pushforward along u ↦ u^p − u). Its Frobenius trace at x ∈ F_{q^r} is ψ(Tr_{F_{q^r}/F_q} x) (in the chosen sign convention); L_ψ(z+w) ≅ L_ψ(z)⊗L_ψ(w) under pullback along addition, and L_ψ(−z) ≅ L_{ψ^{-1}}(z).
items.locator: §2, pp.900–901; used in §3, Lemma 3.2, p.910 and §5, Lemma 5.3, p.928 (arXiv v3: p.8; p.17; p.33)
unitTests: ψ=1 yields the constant sheaf, not an acyclic one
a nontrivial rank-one ψ need not exist over Q_ℓ itself
items.note: Review (REV-PAPER-BROWNING-SAWIN-20): statement corrected against the paper: The paper takes ψ to be any non-trivial additive character of F_q (p.900: 'let ψ be a non-trivial additive character of F_q'; p.901: L_ψ 'associated to the character ψ on F_q'), not only a character of F_p. The item's construction along u ↦ u^p − u only produces the sheaves of characters of F_p (i.e. ψ0∘Tr). Harmless, since every ψ is x ↦ ψ0(Tr(ax)) and then L_ψ = [x↦ax]^*L_{ψ0∘Tr}, but the definition should say so or use the Lang torsor u ↦ u^q − u. Review note: Owner FF (source route to FiniteFieldsAndCharacterSums:FF.2) is reasonable; no atlas stage constructs L_ψ explicitly.

items.name: Geometric exponential-sum complex
items.statement: For p2:A^{dn}×A^L→A^L set S_{d,f}=Rp2! e*L_ψ. Its geometric stalk at b is RΓ_c(A^{dn},L_ψ(e(−,b))).
unitTests: b=0 stalk E[−2dn](−dn)
do not replace ! by ordinary pushforward

items.name: Cohomological Fourier orthogonality
items.statement: H_c^i(Mor_{d,x},E)≅H_c^{i+2kd}(A^{kd},S_{d,f})(kd), compatibly with Frobenius over F_q. Integrating the L linear phase variables gives zero off the coefficient-zero locus and E[−2L](−L) on it.
items.locator: §2, Lemma 2.1, p.901; proof pp.901–902, citing [16, Lemma 13] = Katz, 'Sums of Betti numbers' ([15] in arXiv v3) (arXiv v3: pp.8–9)

items.name: Hankel-rank geometric major arcs
items.statement: For 0≤m≤L, A_m^L⊂A^L is cut out by rank((b_{i+j−1})_{1≤i≤L−m,1≤j≤m+1})≤m. Set A_{−1}=∅ and A_m=A^L for m>L. Distinguish closed subschemes from their underlying reduced strata when using dimensions.
items.locator: §2, Definition 2.3, p.903 (arXiv v3: p.10)
unitTests: m=0 gives b=0
L=9,m=4,b5=1 gives an invertible 5×5 matrix
items.note: Review note: The convention A_m = A^L for m > L is the extraction's reading of the printed '(kd−m)×(m+1) matrix' for m > kd (E27, confirmed).

items.name: Closedness and nesting of major arcs
items.statement: A_m^L is closed and A_m^L⊂A_{m+1}^L for every nonnegative m; A_0={0}.

items.name: Exact automatic-full range
items.statement: A_m^L=A^L for m≥ceil(L/2). For odd L the preceding A_floor(L/2)^L need not be full.
items.locator: §2, Lemma 2.4(3), p.903; corrected use in §5, proof of Proposition 2.6, p.934 (arXiv v3: p.10; p.38)
items.note: Review note: REPAIR VERDICT: sound. For m ≥ L/2 the Hankel matrix has L−m ≤ m rows, so its rank is ≤ m and A_m = A^L; since m is an integer this is m ≥ ⌈L/2⌉, exactly Lemma 2.4(3). For L = 2t+1 the matrix at m = t is (t+1)×(t+1), and b_{t+1} = 1, all other b_r = 0 gives the anti-identity (rank t+1), so A_t ≠ A^L (checked for L = 9, m = 4). This supports E1's replacement of m0 = ⌊kd/2⌋−1 by ⌈kd/2⌉−1 in the §5 stratification (E1 itself lies in §5 and is left to that reviewer).

items.name: Hankel rank and Padé approximation
items.statement: For m≤L and b∈A^L, b∈A_m iff there are 0≤m'≤m, monic h2 of degree m', and h1 of degree <m', such that Σ_{r≤L}b_rT^{−r}=h1/h2+O(T^{−L−1+m−m'}). Here O means all exponents at most the indicated exponent.
items.locator: §2, Lemma 2.4(4), p.903; proof p.904 (arXiv v3: pp.10–11)

items.name: Unique reduced approximation on a rank stratum
items.statement: If 0≤m≤L/2 and b∈A_m\A_{m−1}, the triple (m',h1,h2) in padeexist is unique, h1,h2 are coprime, and if m'<m the coefficient at T^{−L−1+m−m'} in the error is nonzero.
items.locator: §2, Lemma 2.4(5), p.903; proof pp.904–905 (arXiv v3: p.11)

items.name: Exact-denominator major-arc open
items.statement: For 0≤m≤L/2 define U_m^L⊂A_m\A_{m−1} by the existence of coprime h1,h2 with h2 monic of exact degree m and b=h1/h2+O(T^{−L−1}). This fixes all L Laurent coefficients.
unitTests: a lower-degree denominator belongs to the boundary, not U_m
items.note: Review note: The printed definition does not require gcd(h1,h2) = 1 (only deg h1 < m, h2 monic of degree m); for m ≤ L/2 and b ∉ A_{m−1} coprimality is automatic by Lemma 2.4(5), so the item is equivalent.

items.name: Polynomial-pair model of the good arc
items.statement: For 0 ≤ m ≤ L/2: U_m^L is Zariski open in A_m^L, and the coefficients of (h1,h2) are regular on U_m^L and give an isomorphism U_m^L ≅ {(h1,h2): h2 monic of degree m, deg h1 < m, gcd(h1,h2) = 1}, an open subscheme of A^{2m}; hence dim U_m^L = 2m (U_0 = {0}). Moreover dim(A_m^L \ A_{m−1}^L) ≤ 2m, hence dim A_m^L ≤ 2m, because by Lemma 2.4(4)–(5) each point of the stratum is determined by (m', h1, h2) with m' ≤ m together with the m − m' error coefficients at T^{−L−1+m−m'}, …, T^{−L}, i.e. by at most m + m' ≤ 2m parameters.
items.locator: §3, Lemma 3.1, pp.908–909; proof pp.909–910; dimension use in §5, proof of Proposition 2.6, p.934 (arXiv v3: pp.15–16; p.38)
items.note: Review (REV-PAPER-BROWNING-SAWIN-20): statement corrected against the paper: Lemma 3.1 assumes m ≤ kd/2; the item should state 0 ≤ m ≤ L/2 in its first sentence (item goodarc restricts the domain, so this is implicit). The last clause (dim A_m ≤ 2m) is not part of Lemma 3.1: it is the dimension bound used without proof in §5, p.934 ('a variety of dimension 2(m+1)'). It is true, and follows from Lemma 2.4(4)–(5) by counting parameters, which the item should say.

items.name: Cancellation along a nontrivial additive orbit
items.statement: Let Y be a variety over a separably closed field of characteristic p, φ:Y→A1, u∈O(Y)×, and a:G_a×Y→Y an action with φ(a(λ,y))=φ(y)+u(y)λ. Then RΓ_c(Y,φ*L_ψ)=0. Prove u is orbit-invariant and normalize the orbit coordinate by u.
items.locator: §3, Lemma 3.2, p.910 (arXiv v3: pp.16–17)
items.note: Review note: The printed proof has the Künneth degree misprint E11 (confirmed); the statement is unaffected.

items.name: Lower-denominator boundary cancellation
items.statement: For 0≤m≤d the stalks of S_{d,f} vanish on (A_m^L\A_{m−1}^L)\U_m^L. Hence its compact cohomology on the stratum equals that on U_m.
items.locator: §3, Lemma 3.3, p.911; proof pp.911–912 (arXiv v3: pp.17–18)

items.name: Remainder fibration on the good arc
items.statement: For 0≤m≤d the polynomial remainder map ρ:A^{dn}×U_m→A^{mn}×U_m, g↦g mod h2, is an affine-space bundle of dimension n(d−m). The phase factors as e=ebar∘ρ.
items.locator: §3, pp.912–913, and proof of Lemma 3.4, p.913 (arXiv v3: pp.18–19)
unitTests: m=d gives relative dimension zero
m>d is excluded

items.name: Residue-class exponential complex
items.statement: Let p2':A^{mn}×U_m→U_m and π2:U_m→A^m, (h1,h2)↦h2. Set Sbar_{m,f}=Rπ2! Rp2'! ebar*L_ψ on the space of monic degree-m polynomials.
unitTests: Sbar_0=E
Rπ2! cannot be treated as a sheaf on U_m

items.name: Affine-fibre shift and twist
items.statement: Rρ!E=E[−2n(d−m)](−n(d−m)); H_c^i(U_m,S)=H_c^{i−2n(d−m)}(A^m,Sbar_m)(−n(d−m)) for m≤d.
items.locator: §3, Lemma 3.4, p.913; proof pp.913–914 (arXiv v3: pp.19–20)
items.note: Review note: The item's Rρ_!E = E[−2n(d−m)](−n(d−m)) is the correct form of the printed display (E12, confirmed).

items.name: Coprime multiplicativity
items.statement: Over pairs of coprime monic l1,l2 of degrees m1,m2, pullback of Sbar_{m1+m2} along multiplication is Sbar_{m1}⊠Sbar_{m2}. The isomorphism uses g modulo l1,l2 and h1=h11*l2+h12*l1; it is symmetric under swapping the two factors with the derived Koszul symmetry.
items.locator: §3, Lemma 3.5, p.914; proof pp.914–915 (arXiv v3: pp.20–21)
items.note: Review note: The symmetry clause makes sense only for m1 = m2, as in the paper; the printed proof says 'switching h1 and h2' for l1, l2 (E13, confirmed).

items.name: Nonsquarefree-modulus cancellation
items.statement: If X is smooth and h2 is monic nonsquarefree, the stalk of Sbar_m at h2 is zero. Reduce to h2=(T−a)^r, r≥2, and distinguish f(g(a))=0 (use a nonzero gradient) from f(g(a))≠0 (translate h1).
items.locator: §3, Lemma 3.6, p.916; proof pp.916–917 (arXiv v3: pp.21–22)

items.name: Reduced compact cohomology via trace fibre
items.statement: For smooth geometrically irreducible X of dimension n−1 define RΓ_c,red(X,E)=fib(RΓ_c(X,E)→E[−2(n−1)](−(n−1))). The map is the smooth trace and induces an isomorphism in top degree.
unitTests: X=A^{n−1} gives an acyclic fibre
non-geometrically-irreducible X needs a componentwise trace target

items.name: One-parameter exponential cohomology
items.statement: For the smooth X in the standing hypotheses, RΓ_c(G_m×A^n,L_ψ(h f(a)))≅RΓ_c,red(X,E)[−2](−1). The proof uses the zero locus in the G_a-parameter calculation and surjectivity of the relevant trace map.
items.locator: §3, Lemma 3.7, p.917; proof pp.917–918, citing [15, 8.2.5(2)] = Katz, GKSM ([16] in arXiv v3) (arXiv v3: pp.23–24)
items.note: Review note: The paper's hypothesis 'X irreducible' is automatic under the standing hypotheses (new issue on geometric irreducibility of X); the item's 'standing hypotheses' reading is right.

items.name: Linear-modulus constant complex
items.statement: Sbar_{1,f} on A1 is the constant complex with value RΓ_c,red(X,E)[−2](−1). Translation of the unique root gives the canonical model.
items.locator: §3, Lemma 3.8, p.918 (arXiv v3: p.24)

items.name: Configuration-space descent for all moduli
items.statement: RΓ_c(A^m,Sbar_m)≅(RΓ_c(PConf_m,E)⊗RΓ_c,red(X,E)^{⊗m})^{S_m}[−2m](−m). Use repeated-modulus vanishing, CRT and the finite étale root-ordering torsor; invariants are exact over E.
items.locator: §3, Lemma 3.9, p.918; proof p.919 (arXiv v3: p.24)

items.name: Major-arc stratum complex
items.statement: For 0≤m≤d, RΓ_c(A_m\A_{m−1},S)≅(RΓ_c(PConf_m)⊗RΓ_c,red(X)^{⊗m})^{S_m}[−2m−2n(d−m)](−m−n(d−m)). The m≤d condition is essential.
items.locator: §3, Corollary 3.10, p.919 (arXiv v3: pp.24–25)
items.note: Review note: The printed Corollary 3.10 omits 0 ≤ m ≤ d (E16, confirmed and still present in print); the item's restriction is the correct statement.

items.name: Reduced cohomology concentrated in the middle
items.statement: Under smoothness of X and of its degree-k projective boundary, H_c,red^i(X,E)=0 for i≠n−1, and H_c,red^{n−1}=H_c^{n−1}. Use affine vanishing and weak Lefschetz on Xbar and Z.
items.locator: §3, Lemma 3.11, p.919; proof pp.919–920 (arXiv v3: pp.25–26)

items.name: Explicit cohomology of each major-arc stratum
items.statement: For 0≤m≤d, H_c^i(A_m\A_{m−1},S)≅(H_c^{i+m(n−1)−2nd}(PConf_m,E)⊗V^{⊗m}⊗sgn^{n−1})^{S_m}(−m−n(d−m)).
items.locator: §3, Corollary 3.12, p.920 (arXiv v3: p.26)

items.name: Universal smooth polynomial and boundary-point family
items.statement: M_{n,k} parametrizes (f,x) with f degree k, X and Z smooth, x≠0 and f0(x)=0. Let pr_{M,X}:𝓧→M be the universal affine hypersurface; h_n and h_{n−1} send (f,x) to the projective homogenization and leading-form hypersurfaces.
unitTests: rescaling f preserves X but changes the parameter point
projectivizing x forgets a G_m fibre

items.name: Primitive universal hypersurface local system
items.statement: For the parameter space H_{r,k} of smooth degree-k hypersurfaces in P^r, Prim_{r,k} is the primitive part of R^{r−1}π!E. In even cohomological degree split off the ambient hyperplane-class Tate line using its nonzero self-intersection.
items.locator: §4, p.922; rank formula used in the proof of Lemma 4.3, p.924 (arXiv v3: p.27; p.29)
unitTests: r=2 gives a symplectic H1
quadrics have primitive rank 0 or 1 depending on parity

items.name: Universal affine compact-cohomology support
items.statement: R^i pr_{M,X}!E vanishes except in degrees n−1 and 2(n−1), is lisse in those degrees, and R^{2(n−1)}=E(−(n−1)).

items.name: Extension by boundary and projective primitives
items.statement: There is an exact sequence 0→h_{n−1}*Prim_{n−1,k}→R^{n−1}pr_{M,X}!E→h_n*Prim_{n,k}→0. Prove via localization and hyperplane classes, separately for the parity of n.
items.locator: §4, Lemma 4.2(2), p.923; proof p.923 (arXiv v3: pp.27–28)

items.name: Full universal hypersurface monodromy
items.statement: Let k ≥ 3, r ≥ 2 and let p = char of the base field satisfy p ≠ ℓ and p odd (p > k suffices for the paper), with (r−1, k) ≠ (2, 3). Over the parameter space H_{r,k} of smooth degree-k hypersurfaces in P^r, the geometric (Zariski) monodromy group of Prim_{r,k} is Sp_N if r−1 is odd and the full orthogonal group O_N if r−1 is even (N = rank Prim_{r,k}) [Katz–Sarnak, Th. 11.4.9]. For k = 2 the primitive part has rank 0 or 1 and is treated directly.
items.locator: §4, proof of Lemma 4.3, p.924, citing [17, Th. 11.4.9] (arXiv v3: p.29)
items.note: Review (REV-PAPER-BROWNING-SAWIN-20): statement corrected against the paper: 'Over every geometric characteristic ≠ ℓ' claims more than the paper uses or checks: Lemma 4.3 is applied only under the standing hypothesis p > k ≥ 3 (so p odd). The characteristic hypotheses of Katz–Sarnak 11.4.9, in particular p = 2 for even-dimensional hypersurfaces, must be read before the item is stated for all p ≠ ℓ. Review note: Missing is right: LefschetzPencilsAndVanishingCycles:LPV.5 proves only the odd-dimensional symplectic open image for a pencil, not the universal O/Sp statement.

items.name: Monodromy pullback along the universal pair maps
items.statement: For n≥3, h_n and h_{n−1} are smooth with geometrically connected generic fibres, and their normal targets give surjections on geometric étale fundamental groups. Include the scalar and nonzero-vector factors omitted from the informal description when constructing the maps.
items.locator: §4, proof of Lemma 4.3, p.924 (arXiv v3: p.29)

items.name: Orthogonal–symplectic product criterion
items.statement: Over an algebraically closed characteristic-zero coefficient field, a closed subgroup of O_a×Sp_b projecting onto both factors is the full product when a≥6 and the orthogonal and symplectic simple quotients have no exceptional isomorphism. Handle b=0 and disconnected O separately; use algebraic-group Goursat, not only abstract-group Goursat.
items.locator: §4, proof of Lemma 4.3, pp.924–925 (arXiv v3: p.29)
items.note: Review note: For a ≥ 6 no so(a) is isomorphic to any sp(b), so the second clause is redundant. The printed exceptional pairs are reversed (E18, confirmed).

items.name: A monodromy element with only eigenvalue minus one
items.statement: For k≥2,n≥3,(k,n)≠(3,3),(3,4), geometric monodromy of R^{n−1}pr_{M,X}!E contains an element all of whose eigenvalues are −1. It need not be the scalar −Id on the nonsplit extension; generalized eigenspaces suffice.
items.locator: §4, Lemma 4.3, p.923; proof pp.924–925 (arXiv v3: pp.28–29)

items.name: Relative stratum formula and lissity
items.statement: For 0≤m≤d, R^i pr_{M,m}!S≅(H_c^{i+m(n−1)−2nd}(PConf_m,E)⊗(R^{n−1}pr_{M,X}!E)^{⊗m}⊗sgn^{n−1})^{S_m}(−m−n(d−m)); all these sheaves are lisse.
items.locator: §4, Lemma 4.4, p.925; proof pp.925–926 (arXiv v3: pp.29–31)
items.note: Review note: The printed Lemma 4.4 has no restriction on m, and its trace target has the twist misprint E19. The item's 0 ≤ m ≤ d is correct (new issue, parallel to E16).

items.name: Odd-page differential vanishing in the verified parameter range
items.statement: For n≥3,k≥2,(k,n)≠(3,3),(3,4), the finite major-arc spectral sequence has d_r=0 for every odd r: a universal monodromy element has eigenvalue (−1)^m on column m and the opposite eigenvalue on column m+r. Restrict the standalone proposition to these hypotheses until its omitted exceptional cases are supplied; all main-theorem parameters satisfy them.
items.locator: §4, Proposition 4.1, p.922, proof pp.926–927; §2, Proposition 2.5(3), p.905 (arXiv v3: p.26, proof pp.30–31; p.12)
items.note: Review note: The restriction matches E23 (confirmed). Also state the standing hypotheses (X and Z smooth, char F_q = p > k, 0 ≤ m ≤ d).

items.name: Finite closed-filtration spectral sequence with convergence
items.statement: For a bounded constructible complex F on Y filtered by finitely many closed Y_{−1}=∅⊂Y0⊂⋯⊂Yd=Y, construct E1^{m,s}=H_c^{m+s}(Y_m\Y_{m−1},F), d_r:(m,s)↦(m+r,s−r+1), and the exhaustive finite filtration on H_c^{m+s}(Y,F). Page/homology data alone do not prove convergence.
items.locator: §2, Proposition 2.5(1), p.905; construction and E1 identification in §3, p.921 (arXiv v3: p.12; p.26)
items.note: Review note: Planned is acceptable but incomplete. FoundationsAndLibraryIntegration:LI.3 supplies the algebraic spectral sequence of a finitely filtered complex; the filtration of RΓ_c(Y,F) by RΓ_c of the open complements and the excision identification of the graded pieces come from the localization triangles of EtaleDualityAndPerverseSheaves:EDC.0 / SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.2, so cite those too. The relative version over M_{n,k} used in the proof of Proposition 4.1 (p.926) is a proposed new item (coverage).

items.name: Major-arc first page before the global shift
items.statement: For 0≤m≤d, E1^{m,s}=(H_c^{s+mn−2nd}(PConf_m,E)⊗V^{⊗m}⊗sgn^{n−1})^{S_m}(−m−n(d−m)); outside this column range it is zero. It converges to H_c^{m+s}(A_d,S).
items.locator: §2, Proposition 2.5(1)–(2), p.905; proof completed in §3, pp.921–922 (arXiv v3: p.12; p.26)

items.name: Finite-difference constancy locus with an explicit order
items.statement: For polynomial G:A^N→A1 and integer k≥1 with deg G≤k, let V_k(G)⊂(A^N)^{k−1} consist of tuples y for which Δ_{y1}⋯Δ_{y{k−1}}G(x) is independent of x. Define dd_k(G)=dim V_k(G), allowing −∞. The parameter k is part of the data even when deg G<k.
items.locator: §5, Definition 5.1 and (5.1), p. 927 (arXiv v3: pp. 31–32)
unitTests: k=1 and nonconstant affine G gives V empty
if deg G<k then V is the whole parameter space
items.note: Review note: Missing; owner GCM (part-ii GeometricCircleMethodAndMappingSpaces); no atlas stage plans it. The statement matches print: the printed alternating sum Σ_ε(−1)^{Σε}G(x+Σε_r y^{(r)}) equals (−1)^{k−1}Δ_{y1}⋯Δ_{y_{k−1}}G(x), so it is constant exactly when the iterated difference is. Making the order k an explicit parameter is needed, not cosmetic. Print defines V(G) only for deg G = k but applies dd(G) to deg G ≤ k (Prop. 5.5 and its induction). If V is formed with deg G differencing steps, Prop. 5.5 is false: for G = x_1^2 in N ≥ 2 variables and k = 3, the degree-2 locus has dimension N−1 and gives the bound (3N−1)/2 < 2N−1 = cd(G), while V_3(G) = (A^N)^2 gives 2N. Recorded as a new misprint.

items.name: Exponential compact-cohomological degree
items.statement: cd_ψ(G)=sup{i∈Z:H_c^i(A^N,L_ψ(G))≠0}, with value −∞ for an acyclic complex. The value is unchanged by coefficient-field extension and polynomial coordinate isomorphisms.
items.locator: §5, Definition 5.2, p. 928; used in the proof of Proposition 5.5, pp. 930–932 (arXiv v3: p. 32)
unitTests: constant phase has cd=2N
nonconstant affine-linear phase has cd=−∞
items.note: Review note: Missing; owner GCM. Matches print. Cohomology is geometric (over F̄_q), as in the extraction's conventions; the stalk formula in the proof of Prop. 5.8 (p. 933) confirms this. Invariance under extension of the coefficient field is the step used in the proof of Lemma 5.3 (p. 929).

items.name: Sign reversal by coefficient conjugation
items.statement: If ℓ has even order modulo p, cd_ψ(G)=cd_ψ(−G). A power of the unramified coefficient-field Frobenius on Q_ℓ(μ_p) sends μ_p to its inverse, giving semilinear cohomology isomorphisms.
items.locator: §5, Lemma 5.3 and proof, pp. 928–929 (arXiv v3: p. 33)
items.note: Review note: Missing; owner GCM. Matches print: ℓ^r ≡ −1 mod p, and Frob_ℓ^r ∈ Gal(Q_ℓ(μ_p)/Q_ℓ) (unramified, since ℓ ≠ p) sends L_ψ(G) to L_{ψ^{-1}}(G) = L_ψ(−G), which gives a semilinear isomorphism on every H^i_c.

items.name: Tensor-product and difference identities for cohomological degree
items.statement: cd(G)+cd(−G)=cd(G(x)−G(y))=cd(G(x)−G(x+y)); use the compact-support Künneth formula and an invertible triangular coordinate change. Interpret all identities in Z∪{−∞}.
items.locator: §5, Lemma 5.4 and proof, p. 929 (arXiv v3: p. 33)
items.note: Review note: Missing; owner GCM. Matches print: Künneth for H_c with field coefficients, then the invertible substitution x_{N+i} ↦ x_i + x_{N+i}.

items.name: Geometric Weyl-differencing bound
items.statement: For G in N variables of degree ≤k over F_q, p>k and ℓ of even order modulo p, cd(G)≤[dd_k(G)+N(2^{k−1}−(k−1))]/2^{k−2}. Include k=1 and all acyclic fibres; prove by differencing, projection, support dimension and induction.
items.locator: §5, Proposition 5.5, p. 930; proof pp. 930–932 (arXiv v3: pp. 34–35)
items.note: Review note: Missing; owner GCM. Matches print (ℓ of even order mod p; deg G ≤ k; §5's standing p > k). Proof rechecked. The supremum over 0 ≤ r ≤ N of 2r + (dd − r + N(2^{k−2} − (k−2)))/2^{k−3} is attained at r = N and equals (dd + N(2^{k−1} − (k−1)))/2^{k−3}; the base case gives 2N; empty fibres give −∞, consistently. The proof's printed 𝔸^n × 𝔸^n, 𝔸^n × W_j and G(x_1,…,x_n) should read N (new misprint). The fibre-dimension stratification it uses ([13, Ex. II.3.22(e)]) has no item; see coverage.

items.name: Top-degree multilinear polarization
items.statement: In p>k write G_k(x)=Σ c_{i1,…,ik}x_i1⋯x_ik with symmetric c. The coefficients of x in the (k−1)-fold difference are k! times the corresponding symmetric multilinear forms. Thus V_k(G)=V_k(G_k) is cut out by N multilinear equations.
items.locator: §5, paragraph after the proof of Proposition 5.5, p. 932 (arXiv v3: pp. 35–36)
unitTests: p dividing k! is excluded
adding lower-degree terms does not change V_k
items.note: Review note: Missing; routed to ES.0–1 (source). Verified: for G_k = Σ a_i x_{i1}⋯x_{ik} with a symmetric, the part of the (k−1)-fold difference that is linear in x is ±k!·Σ_i (Σ a_{i1…i_{k−1} i} y^{(1)}_{i1}⋯y^{(k−1)}_{i_{k−1}}) x_i. Parts of lower degree contribute constants. p > k makes both k! and the symmetrisation of monomial coefficients invertible. The identity also holds for k = 1.

items.name: All-extension point bounds detect dimension
items.statement: Let V be finite type over F_q. If one constant C satisfies #V(F_{q^r})≤C q^{rD} for every r≥1, then dim V≤D. Apply Lang–Weil on an irreducible component after its finite field of definition; a bound only over F_q is insufficient.
items.locator: §5, Lemma 5.6 and proof, p. 932 (arXiv v3: p. 36)
items.note: Review note: Missing; routed to FF.2 (source). The item generalises Lemma 5.6 (stated for V(G)) to any V of finite type over F_q. The generalisation is true and is exactly what the printed proof uses: a top-dimensional geometrically irreducible component is defined over some F_{q^{r0}}, and Lang–Weil over F_{q^{r0 r}} gives q^{r0 r·dim}(1+o(1)) ≤ C q^{r0 r D}.

items.name: Lang–Weil lower asymptotic needed by differencing
items.statement: For geometrically irreducible finite-type V/F_Q of dimension e, #V(F_{Q^r})=Q^{re}+O_V(Q^{r(e−1/2)}) as r→∞ (with the zero-dimensional case separate). An irreducible geometric component descends to a finite extension. Only this input, not smooth-projective RH alone, proves extensiondimension.
items.locator: §5, proof of Lemma 5.6, p. 932, citing [18] Lang–Weil, Amer. J. Math. 76 (1954), 819–827 (arXiv v3: p. 36)
items.note: Review note: Missing; routed to FF.2 (source). No stage of data/atlas.json names Lang–Weil (a search for 'Lang[–-]Weil|Lang and Weil' returns nothing), and FF.2's description (Weil and Deligne exponential-sum bounds) does not mention it. The FF.2 packet must therefore take it on explicitly. The statement is the standard Lang–Weil estimate.

items.name: Differencing-dimension bound outside a rank arc
items.statement: For d≥k−1, d≤m≤kd/2 and b∉A_m^{kd}, the degree-≤k polynomial G_b(a)=e(a,b) in dn variables satisfies dd_k(G_b)≤dn(k−1)−n floor(m/(k−1)), assuming smooth f0 and p>k.
items.locator: §5, Proposition 5.7, p. 933; proof completed in §6 after Proposition 6.2, p. 937 (arXiv v3: p. 37)
items.note: Review note: Missing; owner GCM. Matches print: smooth leading form, char > k, d ≥ k−1, d ≤ m ≤ kd/2, and every r ≥ 1 with b ∈ (A^{kd} \ A_m)(F_{q^r}). Here k ≥ 3 is only a standing hypothesis, but Prop. 6.2, on which the proof rests, states it explicitly; the extraction's conventions include it.

items.name: Stalk cohomology supported on a major arc
items.statement: Assume f_0 defines a smooth hypersurface in P^{n−1}, char F_q = p > k ≥ 3, ℓ has even order mod p, and m ≥ d ≥ k−1. Then for every i > n(2d − ⌊m/(k−1)⌋/2^{k−2}) the cohomology sheaf H^i(S_{d,f}) vanishes on A^{kd} \ A_m^{kd}. For m ≥ kd/2 this is vacuous. For d ≤ m ≤ kd/2 it follows from Props. 5.5 and 5.7, the stalk formula (S_{d,f})_b̄ = RΓ_c(A^{dn}_{F̄_q}, L_ψ(G_b)), and closed-point detection of constructible supports.
items.locator: §5, Proposition 5.8 and proof, pp. 933–934 (arXiv v3: p. 37)
items.note: Review (REV-PAPER-BROWNING-SAWIN-20): statement corrected against the paper: Print states Prop. 5.8 for every m ≥ d ≥ k−1, with no upper bound on m. The item's 'same range' imports the bound m ≤ kd/2 from item 50. The restriction is harmless, because for m ≥ kd/2 we have A_m = A^{kd} (Lemma 2.4(3)) and the claim is vacuous, but the item is formally weaker than print. The smoothness and p > k hypotheses are only inherited by reference. Review note: Missing; owner GCM. The final step of the proof has no item: a constructible support defined over F_q that has no F_{q^r}-points for any r is empty. See coverage.

items.name: Correct finite stratification of the minor arcs
items.statement: A^L\A_d=⊔_{m=d}^{ceil(L/2)−1}(A_{m+1}\A_m). The top index is a ceiling minus one; replacing it by floor(L/2)−1 misses the last stratum when L is odd.
items.locator: §5, proof of Proposition 2.6 (end of §5), p. 934 (arXiv v3: p. 38); corrected (print has m_0 = ⌊kd/2⌋ − 1; E1)
items.note: Review note: REPAIR VERDICT: sound. The chain A_d ⊆ A_{d+1} ⊆ … ⊆ A_{⌈L/2⌉} = A^L comes from Lemma 2.4(2),(3), and (3) gives fullness exactly for m ≥ L/2. It yields the disjoint decomposition with top index ⌈L/2⌉ − 1, which is empty when d ≥ ⌈L/2⌉. The item's claim that the index ⌊L/2⌋ − 1 misses a stratum when L is odd is also correct. For m = (L−1)/2 the Hankel matrix is square of size (L+1)/2, and b_{(L+1)/2} = 1 with all other b_r = 0 gives the anti-identity, of rank m+1. So A_{(L−1)/2} ≠ A^L; L = 9, b_5 = 1 is the instance in E1. The added stratum m = ⌈L/2⌉ − 1 ≤ L/2 lies in the range (5.2), so Props. 5.7–5.8 apply to it.

items.name: Conservative minor-arc vanishing with rounding retained
items.statement: Under the main hypotheses, H_c^j(A^L\A_d,S)=0 for j>2dn+4(k−1)−4tδ. Indeed each stratum has upper cohomological bound B(m)=2dn−n floor(m/(k−1))/2^{k−2}+4(m+1); writing m=(k−1)q+r yields B(m)=2dn−4qδ+4(r+1)≤2dn−4tδ+4(k−1). This is the proved arithmetic correction to the displayed method, conditional on its geometric intermediate inputs.
items.locator: §2, Proposition 2.6, p. 905; proof at the end of §5, p. 934 (arXiv v3: pp. 12, 38); conservative repair
items.note: Review note: REPAIR VERDICT: sound. Rechecked. The stratum A_{m+1} \ A_m has dimension ≤ 2(m+1), and Prop. 5.8 bounds its cohomology sheaves by n(2d − ⌊m/(k−1)⌋/2^{k−2}). So H^j_c vanishes for j > B(m) = n(2d − ⌊m/(k−1)⌋/2^{k−2}) + 4(m+1). Using n/2^{k−2} = 4(δ + k − 1) and writing m = (k−1)q + r with 0 ≤ r ≤ k−2 gives B(m) = 2dn − 4qδ + 4(r+1). Since m ≥ d forces q ≥ t, and δ > 0 because n > 2^k(k−1), we get B(m) ≤ 2dn − 4tδ + 4(k−1). Excision along the corrected chain (minorcover) finishes the proof. Remarks: (i) for odd L the last stratum has 2(m+1) = L+1, outside goodarciso's clause 'dim A_m ≤ 2m when 2m ≤ L', but its dimension is at most L < 2(m+1), so the bound still holds. (ii) The method cannot do better than this. Its maximum over strata is exactly 2dn − 4tδ + 4(k−1) in every admissible case except (k,d) = (3,2), where the only stratum is m = d = 2 and it gives the sharp 2dn + 4 − 4tδ.

items.name: Unclosed sharp minor-arc target
items.statement: Target stated in Prop.2.6: under the main hypotheses, H_c^j(A^L\A_d,S)=0 for j>2dn+4−4tδ. The proof printed on p.38 does not establish it. No unconditional certification is made: a new estimate improving the rounding remainder is required. Use minorsafe until that input exists.
items.locator: §2, Proposition 2.6, p. 905; printed proof p. 934 (arXiv v3: pp. 12, 38)
items.note: Review note: REPAIR VERDICT: sound as a gate. The target is exactly Prop. 2.6 as printed (checked on the p. 905 image), and the printed proof does not establish it (E2 confirmed). Suggested addition to the item: the printed argument does prove the sharp bound in the single case (k,d) = (3,2), where the only stratum is m = d = 2 and k−1 divides d. In every other admissible case the method gives 2dn − 4tδ + 4(k−1), which exceeds 2dn + 4 − 4tδ. Whether the sharp statement is true is open; the paper supplies nothing else.

items.name: Shifted finite-field E1 formula
items.statement: Shift the major-arc complex by 2dn and twist by kd. For 0≤m≤d, E1^{m,s}=(H_c^{s+mn}(PConf_m,E)⊗V^{⊗m}⊗sgn^{n−1})^{S_m}(kd−m−n(d−m)), zero otherwise; d_r has bidegree (r,1−r) and odd r vanish in the main range.
items.note: Review note: REPAIR VERDICT: sound. This is a faithful restatement, not a repair. Shifting Prop. 2.5(2) (E_1 = (H_c^{s+mn−2nd}(PConf_m) ⊗ V^{⊗m} ⊗ sgn^{n−1})^{S_m}(−m−n(d−m))) by 2dn and twisting by kd gives the printed Thm. 2.7(1). The claim that odd pages vanish 'in the main range' is right: n > 2^k(k−1) ≥ 16 avoids the exceptions of oddpages/E23.

items.name: Conservative cohomology comparison range
items.statement: The shifted major-arc spectral sequence converges to a complex whose degree-i cohomology is H_c^{i+2D}(Mor_{d,x},E), Frobenius-equivariantly over F_q, for i>−4(tδ−(k−1)). Use minorsafe, the localization triangle, and orthogonality. Over general K it is a noncanonical vector-space comparison after spreading out the full pair.
items.locator: §2, Theorem 2.7(3) and proof, p. 906; §1, Theorem 1.1, p. 894 (arXiv v3: pp. 2, 12); conservative repaired range
items.note: Review note: REPAIR VERDICT: sound. Suppose j = i + 2dn > 2dn + 4(k−1) − 4tδ. Then H^j_c and H^{j+1}_c of the minor arcs vanish (minorsafe), so excision gives H^j_c(A_d, S(kd)) ≅ H^j_c(A^{kd}, S(kd)), and this is H^{i+2D}_c(Mor) by Lemma 2.1. This is the printed proof with the corrected constant, and it gives i > −4(tδ − (k−1)). The transfer to a general field K is the spreading-out argument with the E24 correction (item 58).

items.name: Original sharp comparison target, explicitly gated
items.statement: Theorems 1.1 and 2.7 claim the preceding comparison for i>−4(tδ−1). Retain that exact target only as conditional on minorsharpgate and coefficient descent/spreading closure; it is not established by this checkpoint.
items.locator: §1, Theorem 1.1, p. 894; §2, Theorem 2.7(3) and (2.3), p. 906 (arXiv v3: pp. 2, 12)
items.note: Review note: REPAIR VERDICT: sound as a gate. The quoted range i > −4(⌊d/(k−1)⌋(n/2^k − k + 1) − 1) matches print on both pages. It follows from minorsharpgate by the printed excision argument, so it is established for (k,d) = (3,2) (see item 54) and open otherwise.

items.name: Spreading out the pair and cohomology
items.statement: Choose a finitely generated subring R⊂K containing coefficients of f AND coordinates x, invert suitable elements for x≠0, degrees and both smoothness conditions, and stratify compact-cohomology pushforwards to obtain a common lisse open for finitely many nonzero degrees. Transport ranks to a closed finite-field point; in characteristic zero also choose p>k with ℓ of even order mod p.
items.locator: §2, spreading-out paragraph after the proof of Theorem 2.7 (the proof of Theorem 1.1), pp. 906–907 (arXiv v3: p. 13)
unitTests: x need not lie in the ring generated by f's coefficients
Spec K need not equal Spec Frac R
items.note: Review note: REPAIR VERDICT: sound (the statement already carries the E24 correction). Missing; owner GCM; constructibility is planned in SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.2. Print takes R to be the Z-algebra generated by the coefficients of f and says 'Spec K is the generic point of Spec R' (p. 906). Both corrections in the item are right: adjoin the leading vector x, and note that Spec K only maps to the generic point. The item keeps print's choice in characteristic zero of a prime p > k with ℓ of even order mod p (for example ℓ a quadratic non-residue).

items.name: Configuration compact-cohomology support
items.statement: For m≥1, H_c^a(PConf_m,E)=0 unless m+1≤a≤2m. Translation gives PConf_m≅A1×(PConf_m/G_a), with the quotient affine smooth of dimension m−1; use affine vanishing, duality and the A1 shift. For m=0 only a=0 survives.
items.locator: §2, proof of Lemma 2.8, p. 907 (arXiv v3: p. 14)
items.note: Review note: Missing; routed to ConfigurationSpacesAndRationalLoops (TOP). Matches print. The E10 misprint ('because PConf_m is affine of dimension m − 1 [2, Exp. XIV, Cor. 3.2]', which should read PConf_m/G_a) is still in print on p. 907.

items.name: E1 support region
items.statement: E1^{m,s} can be nonzero only at (m,s)=(0,0), or 1≤m≤d with −m(n−1)+1≤s≤−m(n−2).
items.note: Review note: Missing; owner GCM. Matches print; the range follows from m+1 ≤ s+mn ≤ 2m.

items.name: Compact cohomology vanishing bands
items.statement: Within the conservative comparison range i>−4(tδ−(k−1)), H_c^{i+2D}(Mor)=0 unless i=0 or 1−m(n−2)≤i≤−m(n−3) for some 1≤m≤d. The original Cor.1.2 asserts this in the sharper gated range.
items.locator: §1, Corollary 1.2, p. 895 (arXiv v3: p. 3); repaired range
items.note: Review note: REPAIR VERDICT: sound. Inside the comparison range, H^{i+2D}_c is an iterated extension of the E_∞^{m,s} with m+s = i, and these are subquotients of E_1^{m,s}. By Lemma 2.8 they vanish unless (m,s) = (0,0), or m ∈ [1,d] and m+s ∈ [1 − m(n−2), −m(n−3)]. The printed hypotheses (char K = 0, or char K > k with ℓ of even order; d ≥ k−1 ≥ 2; n > 2^k(k−1)) must be carried along; the item has them implicitly through comparisonsafe.

items.name: Automatic E1 degeneration near the top
items.statement: For m+s>1−2(n−2)(n−3), E∞^{m,s}=E1^{m,s}. A potentially nonzero r≥2 differential forces m≥r(n−3)+2≥2n−4. To identify these terms with Mor cohomology also impose the applicable comparison range.
items.locator: §1, paragraph after Conjecture 1.3, p. 898 (arXiv v3: p. 5)
items.note: Review note: REPAIR VERDICT: sound. Rechecked the printed argument. A nonzero d_r out of (m,s) needs the support intervals at (m,s) and (m+r, s−r+1) to meet, which means m ≥ r(n−3)+2 ≥ 2n−4 for r ≥ 2 (d_1 = 0 because odd pages vanish). Then m+s ≤ −m(n−3) ≤ −2(n−2)(n−3). Ruling out incoming differentials, whose source has degree m+s−1, gives the stated m+s > 1 − 2(n−2)(n−3). The caveat is correct and needed: print's '2(n−2)(n−3) − 1 cohomology groups' identifies E_∞ with H_c only inside the comparison range, and print does not check that.

items.name: Conservative irreducibility and expected dimension
items.statement: If d≥k−1≥2, p=0 or p>k, and tδ>k−1, then the corrected comparison reaches i=0; Mor_{d,x} is geometrically irreducible of dimension D. Combine top compact cohomology of rank one with the componentwise dimension lower bound. The source's weaker endpoint condition tδ≥1 is not certified.
items.locator: §1, Corollary 1.4, p. 898; §2, Corollary 2.9 and proof, pp. 907–908 (arXiv v3: pp. 6, 14); conservative sufficient hypothesis
items.note: Review note: REPAIR VERDICT: sound. When tδ > k−1 the conservative range i > −4(tδ − (k−1)) contains i = 0. Then H^{i+2D}_c = 0 for i > 0, because the bands of item 61 lie in i ≤ 0 (n > 3). H^{2D}_c ≅ E_∞^{0,0} = E_1^{0,0} is one-dimensional: no other (m,s) has m+s = 0, and no differential enters or leaves (0,0). Every component has dimension ≥ D (kd equations). So M_{K̄} has a unique irreducible component, of dimension D. δ > 0 follows from tδ > k−1, so n > 2^k(k−1) is implied. E3 is confirmed. Worth adding: at the printed endpoint tδ = 1, granting the sharp range, the dimension statement still holds. H^{2dn+1}_c(minor) = 0 makes H^{2D}_c(Mor) surject onto the one-dimensional E_∞^{0,0}, so M is nonempty and of pure dimension D; only irreducibility is left uncertified. The same holds at tδ = k−1 in the conservative range.

items.name: Small-degree excess-dimension example
items.statement: Let n ≥ 3, k ≥ 3 and 1 ≤ d < k−1, and let K be algebraically closed of characteristic 0 or > k. Take f = x_1^{k−1}x_2 + x_2^k + x_3^k + ⋯ + x_n^k + 1 and the leading vector x = (1,0,…,0) of P = (1:0:⋯:0). Then f_0 defines a smooth Z ∋ P and X = {f = 0} is smooth. The closed subscheme M = {g ∈ Mor_{d,x}: g_2 = 0} is isomorphic to A^d × {(g_3,…,g_n): deg g_j ≤ d−1, Σ_{j≥3} g_j^k + 1 = 0}. It is nonempty (constant g_j with Σ c_j^k = −1), and every irreducible component of M has dimension ≥ d(n−k) − d + k − 1 > d(n−k) = D.
items.locator: §1, Remark 1.5, pp. 898–899 (arXiv v3: p. 6)
items.note: Review (REV-PAPER-BROWNING-SAWIN-20): statement corrected against the paper: The hypothesis n ≥ 3 is missing. For n = 2, curves in x_2 = 0 satisfy f(g) = 1, so M = ∅ and there is no dimension lower bound. The item's nonemptiness witness (a constant solution in x_3,…,x_n) needs n ≥ 3. Print's Remark 1.5 omits nonemptiness altogether (new issue). The leading vector should be the explicit representative x = (1,0,…,0). Review note: Missing; owner GCM. Everything except the missing n ≥ 3 was verified. f_0 = x_1^{k−1}x_2 + x_2^k + ⋯ + x_n^k is nonsingular when p ∤ k(k−1), so for p = 0 or p > k, and X is smooth. M ≅ A^d × {(g_3,…,g_n): deg g_j ≤ d−1, Σ g_j^k + 1 = 0} is cut out by k(d−1)+1 equations in d(n−2) variables. So every component has dim ≥ d + d(n−2) − k(d−1) − 1 = D − d + k − 1, which exceeds D when d < k−1.

items.name: Unproved E1-degeneration proposition
items.statement: Define, do not assert, the proposition that H_c^{i+2D}(Mor,E)≅⊕_{m≥0}(H_c^{i+m(n−1)}(PConf_m,E)⊗V^{⊗m}⊗sgn^{n−1})^{S_m} for i>−4(tδ−1), under the main geometric and characteristic hypotheses. Terms beyond m=d vanish in the stated stable range. This is Conjecture1.3, not a theorem.
items.locator: §1, Conjecture 1.3, p. 897 (arXiv v3: p. 5)
unitTests: odd-page vanishing alone does not imply d2=0
items.note: Review note: Missing (a conjecture); owner GCM. Matches print. The extraction's addition 'terms beyond m = d vanish in the stated range' is true. The m-th summand needs 1 − m(n−2) ≤ i ≤ −m(n−3). For m ≥ d+1 we have −m(n−3) ≤ −(d+1)(n−3) < 4 − 4tδ, because 4tδ ≤ dn/((k−1)2^{k−2}) ≤ dn/4 (k ≥ 3) and n > 16.

items.name: Function-field norm and fractional part
items.statement: On F_q((T^{−1})), |Σ_{i≤r}c_iT^i|=q^r for c_r≠0, |0|=0. The fractional part keeps negative powers; ||α|| is its norm. Vector norms are maxima. Strict |u|<q^h for u∈F_q[T] means deg u<h.
items.locator: §6, pp. 935–936 (definitions of |·| and ‖·‖) (arXiv v3: p. 39)
unitTests: |T|=q while the formal-series variable X=T^{-1} has norm q^{-1}
items.note: Review note: Missing; routed to FunctionFieldLatticesAndShrinking (LAT). Print leaves the normalisation of |·| implicit and writes ‖β‖ = |Σ_{i≤−1} b_i t^i| with t for T (p. 936). |T| = q is the only normalisation compatible with |u| < q^d ⇔ deg u < d, as the item says. Library note: Mathlib at 082e2d3 already has the ∞-adic place: RatFunc.inftyValuation (Mathlib/FieldTheory/RatFunc/Valuation.lean:81, with inftyValuation.X = exp 1) and the completion RatFunc.CompletionAtInfty = F((t⁻¹)) (line 138) with its Valued ℤᵐ⁰ instance (line 142). items.name: Polar forms of the leading hypersurface
items.statement: For symmetric coefficients c of f0, set Ψ_j(u^(1),…,u^(k−1))=k!Σ_{j1,…,j{k−1}}c_{j1,…,j{k−1},j}∏_r u_{j_r}^{(r)}. On the diagonal Ψ_j(u,…,u)=(k−1)!∂_j f0(u).
items.locator: §6, definition of Ψ_j, p. 936; the diagonal identity is used in the proof of Proposition 6.2, p. 939 (arXiv v3: p. 39)
unitTests: p>k makes the factorial invertible
smooth Z makes the common diagonal zero locus {0}
items.note: Review note: Missing; routed to ES.0–1. Verified: Ψ_j(u,…,u) = k!Σ c_{j_1…j_{k−1}j} u_{j_1}⋯u_{j_{k−1}} = (k−1)!·∂_j f_0(u).

items.name: Degree-k part of the residue phase
items.statement: The degree-k homogeneous part of G_b(a) equals Σ_{j1,…,jk}Σ_{0≤i1,…,ik<d}c_{j1,…,jk} b_{i1+⋯+ik+1}∏_r a_{i_r,j_r}. The full G_b may have lower-degree terms, but V_k(G_b)=V_k((G_b)_k).
items.locator: §6, the displays G_b = F(a) and F_0(a), p. 935 (arXiv v3: pp. 38–39); corrected full-polynomial identity (E20)
items.note: Review note: REPAIR VERDICT: sound. f − f_0 contributes to G_b only terms of degree ≤ k−1 in a. A term of f_0(g) has degree k in a exactly when all i_r ≤ d−1, and the T^{−1} coefficient of α∏T^{i_r} is b_{Σi_r+1}, with Σi_r + 1 ≤ k(d−1) + 1 ≤ kd. V_k depends only on the degree-k part (item 47). This is exactly the correction E20 needs.

items.name: Function-field differencing count
items.statement: N(α)=#{u=(u^(1),…,u^(k−1))∈F_q[T]^{n(k−1)}: |u^(r)|<q^d and ||α Ψ_j(u)||<q^{−d} for all j}. For 0≤s≤d define N_s by replacing the box q^d by q^{d−s} and the fractional threshold q^{−d} by q^{−d−(k−1)s}.
items.locator: §6, Lemma 6.1 (definition of N(α)), p. 936, and the definition of N_s(α), p. 938 (arXiv v3: pp. 39–42)
unitTests: N_s≥1 from the zero tuple
strict thresholds include neither degree boundary
items.note: Review note: Missing; routed to ES.0–1. Matches print.

items.name: Differencing points equal the arithmetic count
items.statement: For α=Σ_{r=1}^{kd}b_rT^{−r}, #V_k(G_b)(F_q)=N(α). Matching coefficients turns each polarization equation into the vanishing of the first d negative coefficients of αΨ_j.
items.locator: §6, Lemma 6.1 and proof, p. 936 (arXiv v3: pp. 39–40)
items.note: Review note: Missing; routed to ES.0–1. Verified: the T^{−i−1} coefficient of αΨ_j(u) is k!Σ c_{j_1…j_{k−1}j} b_{i_1+⋯+i_{k−1}+i+1} ∏z, which matches the V(F_0) equations after dividing by k!. That needs p > k, a hypothesis of Lemma 6.1 that the conventions supply. In the proof the block index and the coefficient index are both called i (new misprint).

items.name: Uniform minor-arc differencing count
items.statement: Assume d ≥ k−1, char F_q = p > k ≥ 3, f_0 defines a smooth hypersurface in P^{n−1}, and m ∈ Z with d ≤ m ≤ kd/2. There is c_{d,k,n} > 0, independent of q, such that N(α) ≤ c_{d,k,n} q^{dn(k−1) − n⌊m/(k−1)⌋} for every b ∈ (A^{kd} \ A_m^{kd})(F_q), where α = Σ_{r=1}^{kd} b_r T^{−r}.
items.locator: §6, Proposition 6.2, p. 936; proof pp. 938–939 (arXiv v3: p. 40)
items.note: Review (REV-PAPER-BROWNING-SAWIN-20): statement corrected against the paper: Print's hypothesis is 'char(F_q) > k ⩾ 3'. The item drops k ≥ 3, which is then covered only by the global conventions. It should also say that b is an F_q-point of A^{kd}. Review note: Missing; routed to ES.0–1. Print's '𝔸^N − A_m^{kd}' is E21 (confirmed).

items.name: Polynomial lattices over the Laurent local field
items.statement: For invertible M∈GL_N(F_q((T^{-1}))), the lattice is M F_q[T]^N. Its adjoint is (M^{-1})^t F_q[T]^N relative to the standard dot pairing. Define successive minima R_i as the least radii with i independent lattice vectors; keep strict/open-ball counting conventions distinct.
items.locator: §6, paragraph before Lemma 6.4, p. 937 (arXiv v3: p. 40)
unitTests: rank one T^a F_q[T] has first minimum q^a
replacing M by a singular matrix is invalid
items.note: Review note: Missing; routed to LAT. The item's F_q[T]^N is the correct reading of print's F_q[T]^n (E26 confirmed on the p. 937 image). Print does not define successive minima; the item's definition is standard. F_q((T^{-1})) is available in Mathlib as RatFunc.CompletionAtInfty (see item 66).

items.name: Ultrametric reduced basis and exact box count
items.statement: A full polynomial lattice has a norm-orthogonal reduced basis with norms R_i. Its number of vectors of norm <q^h is ∏_i max(q^h/R_i,1) when h is integral. The product formula uses the discrete value group and polynomial coefficient counts.
items.locator: §6, proof of Lemma 6.4, p. 938, citing Lee [19, Lemma 3.3.5] (arXiv v3: pp. 41–42)
items.note: Review note: Missing; routed to LAT. Print attributes the product formula N = ∏ max{1, R̂_i^{−1}} to Lee's thesis [19, Lemma 3.3.5], not to [5] §4. The formula checks: in an orthogonal basis v_i with |v_i| = q^{R_i}, |Σc_i v_i| < q^h if and only if deg c_i < h − R_i for every i.

items.name: Adjoint successive-minima duality
items.statement: For a lattice Λ and its adjoint Λ*, ordered minima satisfy R_i(Λ)R_{N+1−i}(Λ*)=1. Prove the nonarchimedean reduced-basis theorem rather than importing Euclidean Minkowski bounds.
items.locator: §6, proof of Lemma 6.4, p. 938: duality of the minima of a lattice and its adjoint, used without citation (Lemma 6.4 refines [5, Lemma 4.2], p. 937) (arXiv v3: p. 41)
items.note: Review note: Missing; routed to LAT. True: if B = E·diag(T^{a_i}) with E ∈ GL_N(F_q[[T^{-1}]]) is a reduced basis, then B^{−T} = E^{−T}·diag(T^{−a_i}) is a reduced basis of the adjoint. The item is right to ask for a proof by reduced bases.

items.name: Symmetric simultaneous-approximation counting function
items.statement: For symmetric γ∈M_n(F_q((T^{-1}))) and integers a,c with c>0, N_{γ,a,c}=#{u∈F_q[T]^n: |u|<q^a, ||γu||<q^{−c}}. The auxiliary polynomial vector eliminating the integer part is unique because c>0.
items.locator: §6, Lemma 6.4 (definition of N_{γ,a,c}), p. 937 (arXiv v3: p. 40)
unitTests: γ=0 gives q^{n max(a,0)}
a≤0 leaves only u=0
items.note: Review note: Missing; routed to LAT. Matches print.

items.name: Duality for the symmetric block lattice
items.statement: For Λ represented by [[T^{−a}I,0],[T^cγ,T^c I]], γ symmetric, the adjoint is isometric to T^{a−c}Λ after sign changes and swapping blocks. Hence R_iR_{2n+1−i}=q^{c−a}.
items.locator: §6, proof of Lemma 6.4, pp. 937–938 (arXiv v3: p. 41)
items.note: Review note: Missing; routed to LAT. Verified t^{c−a}Λ_{a,c}^{−T} = JΛ_{a,c}J^{−1} with J = (0 I; −I 0), which uses γ^T = γ. Hence R̂_i R̂_{2n+1−i} = q^{c−a}.

items.name: Exact symmetric-lattice shrinking inequality
items.statement: For a,c,s∈Z, c>0,s≥0 and γ symmetric, N_{γ,a,c}/N_{γ,a−s,c+s}≤q^{ns+n max(floor((a−c)/2),0)}. Equivalently clear the positive denominator. Derive by separating minima pairs across the unit radius.
items.locator: §6, Lemma 6.4, p. 937; proof pp. 937–938 (arXiv v3: pp. 40–42)
items.note: Review note: Missing; routed to LAT. Matches print. Proof checked: each factor is ≤ min(q^s, max(1, R̂_i^{−1})), and R̂_i ≥ q^{⌈(c−a)/2⌉} for i ≥ n+1. The proof's N_{γ,a−s,c−s} is E22 (confirmed on the p. 938 image).

items.name: Iterated multilinear shrinking
items.statement: In the setting of Nalpha, for integer 0≤s≤d, N(α)≤q^{(k−1)ns}N_s(α). Shrink one vector block at a time; polarization symmetry makes each coefficient matrix symmetric and the floor correction zero.
items.locator: §6, paragraph after Lemma 6.4, p. 938 (arXiv v3: p. 42)
items.note: Review note: Missing; routed to ES.0–1. Print states it for every integer s ≥ 0; the item's 0 ≤ s ≤ d is enough. Verified: the step on block j has a = d and c = d + (j−1)s, so ⌊(a−c)/2⌋ ≤ 0, and each γ is symmetric because c is.

items.name: Minor-arc exclusion forces the shrunken polar values to vanish
items.statement: Take s=d−floor(m/(k−1)). If b∉A_m and u is counted by N_s, then every Ψ_j(u)=0. A nonzero Ψ_j would give a rational approximation to α with denominator degree at most m and the error required by Lem.2.4, contradicting b∉A_m.
items.locator: §6, proof of Proposition 6.2, pp. 938–939 (arXiv v3: pp. 42–43)
items.note: Review note: Missing; routed to ES.0–1. Verified: |r| ≤ q^{(⌊m/(k−1)⌋−1)(k−1)} ≤ q^m. If |rα − a| < q^{−kd+m} with deg r = m'' ≤ m, the 'if' direction of Lemma 2.4(4), with m' = m'', puts b in A_m. That direction holds for every m, so no restriction m ≤ kd/2 is needed here. s = d − ⌊m/(k−1)⌋ ≥ 0 by (5.2).

items.name: Dimension bound for the common polar-zero variety
items.statement: For smooth f0 and p>k, W={Ψ_1=⋯=Ψ_n=0}⊂A^{n(k−1)} has dim W≤n(k−2): its intersection with the diagonal A^n is only 0, and the affine dimension inequality gives the bound.
items.locator: §6, proof of Proposition 6.2, p. 939 (arXiv v3: p. 43)
items.note: Review note: Missing; routed to ES.0–1. Correct. V ∩ Δ is the affine cone over Sing(Z) (by Euler's identity, since p > k), which is {0}. Every component of the multi-cone V contains 0, so the affine dimension theorem gives dim V ≤ (k−2)n. That theorem has no item; see coverage.

items.name: Degree-uniform polynomial point bound
items.statement: For affine V⊂A^N over F_q(T), defined over F_q[T], of dimension e and degree Δ, the number of polynomial points with |u|<q^h is O_{Δ,N}(q^{he}) for integral h≥1, uniformly in q. The application is to W of bounded degree depending only on n,k; dimension zero and h=0 need separate elementary handling.
items.locator: §6, proof of Proposition 6.2, p. 939, citing [4, Lemma 2.8] = Browning–Vishe, GAFA 25 (2015), 671–732 (arXiv:1502.00772, p. 12) (arXiv v3: p. 43)
items.note: Review note: Missing; routed to ES.0–1. Checked against BV15 Lemma 2.8 (arXiv:1502.00772, p. 12). Let V ⊂ A^n_K be affine, defined over O = F_q[t], of degree d ≥ 1 and dimension m ≥ 1. Then #{x ∈ V(O): |x| ≤ q^N} = O_{d,n}(q^{(N+1)m}), with the constant depending only on d and n. The item's form with strict |u| < q^h (h = N+1) is equivalent. The degree of W is bounded in terms of k and n (Bézout).

items.name: Continuous mapping space with prescribed infinity germ
items.statement: For K=C define Hom_{d,P} using continuous maps P1(C)→Xbar, sending ∞ to P, finite points into X, and with local homogeneous coordinates (x1+O(|z|),…,xn+O(|z|),z^d+O(|z|^{d+1})) near z=0. A formal construction must specify the topology and uniformity of germ bounds in families before claiming homotopy equivalences.
items.locator: §7, definition of Hom_{d,P}(C,X) and (7.1), p. 940 (arXiv v3: p. 43)
unitTests: a family of shrinking neighbourhoods is not automatically a uniform homotopy
not the full unrestricted continuous mapping space
The escapingloop example prevents using an unspecified compact-open Hom≃Ω²X equivalence.
items.note: Source leaves topology unspecified. See compacthom for the explicit compact-open interpretation and compactcounter for its obstruction. Review note: missing is right: no atlas stage plans prescribed-germ mapping spaces; the item is routed to GeometricCircleMethodAndMappingSpaces. The item is faithful to (7.1) and rightly insists that the topology is part of the definition. With the subspace compact-open topology, Lemma 7.2 fails (E28 confirmed). Conjecture 7.1 also fails at j = 1 in the Fermat example (see the E28 review).

items.name: Unproved algebraic-to-continuous trace comparison
items.statement: Let X ⊂ C^n be a smooth affine hypersurface of degree k whose projective closure X̄ is smooth. Let P = (x_1:…:x_n:0) ∈ X̄ − X, with the representative (x_1,…,x_n) fixed. Assume d ≥ k−1 ≥ 2, and put D = d(n−k), t = ⌊d/(k−1)⌋ and δ = n/2^k − k + 1. Conjecture 7.1 asserts the following for every integer j with 0 ≤ j < 4(tδ−1). The pairing H_c^{2D−j}(Mor_{d,P}(A^1,X),Q) ⊗ H^j(Hom_{d,P}(C,X),Q) → Q is perfect. The pairing pulls a class back along Mor_{d,P}(A^1,X)(C) → Hom_{d,P}(C,X), cups it into H_c^{2D}(Mor_{d,P}(A^1,X),Q) and applies the trace map. This is a conjecture, not a theorem, and its content depends on the topology chosen for Hom_{d,P}(C,X).
items.locator: §7, Conjecture 7.1, p. 940 (arXiv v3: p. 43)
unitTests: a conjecture is not registered as an instance or axiom
finite-dimensional duality requires the range and irreducibility inputs
The escapingloop example prevents using an unspecified compact-open Hom≃Ω²X equivalence.
items.note: The topology is material: no corrected stronger-topology version is silently substituted into the source conjecture. Review (REV-PAPER-BROWNING-SAWIN-20): statement corrected against the paper: It leaves out Conjecture 7.1's hypothesis d ≥ k−1 ≥ 2, which appears only in the extraction's conventions. It also does not say that the pairing is pull-back along the analytic map Mor_{d,P}(A^1,X)(C) → Hom_{d,P}(C,X), followed by cup product into H_c^{2D}(Mor) and the trace map. Otherwise it matches print. Review note: missing is right; the conjecture must never be registered as an axiom. The note 'the topology is material' is borne out. Take the subspace compact-open topology and the Fermat example k=3, d=2, n=40. There H^1(Hom;Q) ≠ 0, because windingnonzero gives a surjection H_1 → Z. But H_c^{2D−1}(Mor) = 0 by Corollary 1.2 at i = −1, which lies inside both the printed range and the conservative range i > −4. So in this reading the conjecture fails at j = 1. The trace on H_c^{2D} of a possibly singular Mor needs the general trace for irreducible D-dimensional varieties; item trace (100) states only the smooth case.

items.name: Continuous mapping space versus the double loop space
items.statement: When Hom_{d,P} is nonempty, Lem.7.2 claims a homotopy equivalence Hom_{d,P}≃Ω²X. Fix a reference map with the same infinity germ, straighten the germ and glue two discs. Supply uniform-family continuity and the chosen mapping-space topology; this checkpoint has not closed that construction. For the compact-open topology this assertion is false by compactcounter; any corrected endpoint must specify a stronger topology and discharge stronggermgate.
items.locator: §7, Lemma 7.2 and its proof, pp. 940–941 (arXiv v3: pp. 43–44)
items.note: Review note: REPAIR VERDICT: sound. The added claim, that Lemma 7.2 is false for the subspace compact-open topology, is correct. compactcounter (checked at items 120–132) gives π1(Hco,g) ↠ Z, while for Fermat k=3, d=2, n=40 the space Ω²X is connected and simply connected. The failure already shows in H^1(−;Q), the group that Theorem 7.7 uses. The printed proof breaks at the sentence 'this convex combination will not introduce any new zeroes in a neighbourhood': in a family the neighbourhood is not uniform. For the escaping loop at s = 3r(R)/2 the normalised normal coordinate is −1, so the midpoint of the convex combination with z^d vanishes. The status missing is right, and stronggermgate honestly records what remains open.

items.name: Signed Witt–Euler exponents
items.statement: For N≥0 and a fixed parity n, define integers e_r(N) by ∏_{r≥1}(1−T^r)^{−e_r(N)}=1+(−1)^{n−1}NT in Z[[T]]. Coefficients are defined degreewise using only finitely many factors.
items.locator: §7, Definition 7.3, p. 941 (arXiv v3: p. 44)
unitTests: N=0 gives every e_r=0
n odd,N=1 gives e1=1,e2=−1,e_r=0 for r>2
items.note: Review note: missing; routed to ConfigurationSpacesAndRationalLoops. The unit tests were checked: N=0 gives e ≡ 0; n odd and N=1 give e1=1, e2=−1 and e_r=0 for r ≥ 3. The defining identity was also checked by machine up to T^10 for n=4..7 and N ∈ {1,2,3,8}. Print's e_k(N) hides its dependence on the parity of n and reuses k, the degree of the hypersurface, as the product index; the item's r is the better convention.

items.name: Möbius formula for the Euler exponents
items.statement: For r≥1, e_r(N)=−(1/r)Σ_{a|r}μ(a)((−1)^n N)^{r/a}. Use a formal logarithmic derivative and Möbius inversion; show integrality via the defining integer Euler product rather than division in Z without a proof.
items.locator: §7, (7.2) and its derivation, pp. 941–942 (arXiv v3: p. 44)
items.note: Review note: missing; libmobius supplies the Möbius inversion. The printed logarithm step was checked and its sign is right: log of the left side = Σ e_k Σ_d T^{kd}/d = −Σ ((−1)^n N)^m T^m/m.

items.name: Twisted configuration trace formula
items.statement: For a characteristic-zero S_m character χ, Σ_{f monic squarefree,deg f=m}χ(Frob_f)=Σ_a(−1)^a q^{m−a}〈χ,H^a(PConf_m,E)〉=Σ_i(−1)^{m−i}q^i〈χ,H_c^{m+i}(PConf_m,E)〉. The first cohomology is ORDINARY, not compactly supported.
items.locator: §7, proof of Lemma 7.4, p. 942 (arXiv v3: p. 45), citing [6, Th. 3.7]. Print writes H_c in the first two sums (E6); the item's ordinary-cohomology form is the correct one.
items.note: Review note: missing; debt G8 (CEF's imported arrangement cohomology).

items.name: Split hyperplane-complement cohomology
items.statement: For a finite set of hyperplanes defined over F_q in A^m and ℓ≠p, ordinary étale cohomology of their complement is generated by the degree-one hyperplane classes; H^a is a direct sum of E(−a), so Frobenius acts by q^a. Apply to PConf_m and compare with complex cohomology.
items.locator: §7, input to [6, Th. 3.7] in the proof of Lemma 7.4, p. 942 (arXiv v3: p. 45); print cites only [6, Th. 3.7]
items.note: Review note: missing; debt G8. PConf_m needs only the case where every hyperplane x_i = x_j is defined over F_q, so Frobenius acts on H^a by q^a. An S_m-equivariant comparison with the complex Orlik–Solomon algebra is needed as well, for 'the coefficients are independent of q'; the item should say so explicitly.

items.name: Twisted configuration multiplicities by Euler products
items.statement: For V of dimension N, dim(H_c^{m+i}(PConf_m,E)⊗V^{⊗m}⊗sgn^{n−1})^{S_m}=(−1)^{mn+i}[q^i U^m]∏_{r≥1}(1−qU^r)^{−e_r(N)}. The character of V^{⊗m} is N^{number of cycles}; the sign twist changes it by (−1)^{(n−1)(m−cycles)}.
items.locator: §7, Lemma 7.4 and its proof, pp. 942–943 (arXiv v3: pp. 44–45); print's last line drops the exponent −e_k(N) (E7)
items.note: Review note: missing. The reviewer checked the Euler-product step by brute-force enumeration: the sum of ((−1)^{n−1}N)^{ω(f)}(−1)^{(n−1)m} over squarefree monic f of degree m over F_q equals (−1)^{(n−1)m}[U^m]∏(1−qU^k)^{−e_k(N)}. This was checked over F_2 and F_3 for m ≤ 4, n ∈ {4,5} and N ≤ 3. The proof also uses the F_q[t] Euler products and the character-of-invariants formula, which no item covers (see coverage).

items.name: Stable diagonal coefficient identity
items.statement: For integers j,d,N≥0,n>3 and d(n−3)≥j, Σ_{m=0}^d dim(H_c^{mn−m−j}(PConf_m,E)⊗V^{⊗m}⊗sgn^{n−1})^{S_m}=[q^{−j}]∏_{r≥1}(1−(−q)^{1−r(n−2)})^{−e_r(N)}. Extract the relevant weighted diagonal of the two-variable series; it is not the entire series.
items.locator: §7, Corollary 7.5 and its proof, including (7.3), pp. 943–944 (arXiv v3: pp. 45–46)
items.note: Review note: REPAIR VERDICT: sound. The statement is exactly Corollary 7.5 as printed, and the corollary is true. The repair only replaces the false identity (7.3) by coefficient extraction: c_m := [q^{m(n−2)−j}U^m]∏(1−qU^k)^{−e_k(N)}, and c_m ≠ 0 only if m(n−3) ≤ j ≤ d(n−3), so m ≤ d. Substituting U = q^{2−n} is well defined as a series in q^{−1} because 1−k(n−2) ≤ −1 when n ≥ 4, and it gives Σ_m c_m = [q^{−j}]∏(1−q^{1−k(n−2)})^{−e_k}. Replacing q by −q supplies the factor (−1)^j. Checked by machine: (−1)^j Σ_m c_m equals the q^{−j} coefficient for n=4..7, N ∈ {1,2,3,8} and j ≤ 25, and only m with m(n−3) ≤ j contribute.

items.name: Tame polynomial at infinity
items.statement: For a complex polynomial f, use Broughton's gradient criterion: outside a compact subset of C^n the gradient norm is bounded below by a positive constant. A smooth homogeneous leading form implies the stronger growth ||∇f(z)||≥c||z||^{k−1} for sufficiently large ||z|| by compactness of the unit sphere.
items.locator: §7, proof of Lemma 7.6, p. 944 (arXiv v3: p. 46), citing [3]
unitTests: nonisolated leading-gradient zeros prevent this argument
the noncompact fibre need not be projective
items.note: Review note: missing. The growth estimate ‖∇f‖ ≥ c‖z‖^{k−1} for large ‖z‖ is right. A common zero of ∇f_0 other than 0 is a singular point of the projective hypersurface by Euler's formula; compactness of the unit sphere then gives the bound, and lower terms contribute O(‖z‖^{k−2}).

items.name: Smooth tame fibre has the homotopy type of a sphere bouquet
items.statement: For a regular fibre X of a tame complex polynomial in n variables, the source uses Broughton Theorem2 to conclude X≃∨_N S^{n−1}, where N=dim H^{n−1}(X,Q). Exact original-source hypotheses and proof remain to be verified; retain this as an explicit prerequisite gate.
items.locator: §7, proof of Lemma 7.6, p. 944 (arXiv v3: p. 46), citing [3, Th. 2]. Print writes ∧^N S^{n−1} for the wedge (new misprint).
items.note: Review note: missing; source debt G4. In the Fermat special case, fermatjoin (the Pham–Milnor join) gives the bouquet independently.

items.name: Hilton decomposition for an equal-dimensional wedge
items.statement: For n≥3, π_i(∨_N S^{n−1}) decomposes into the finite-degree relevant factors π_i(S^{w(n−2)+1}), with multiplicity (1/w)Σ_{a|w}μ(a)N^{w/a}. The original [14] Cor.4.10 and its wedge/product conventions require verification before implementation.
items.locator: §7, proof of Lemma 7.6, p. 944 (arXiv v3: p. 46), citing [14, Cor. 4.10]
items.note: Review note: missing; debt G4. The restriction n ≥ 3 (simply connected spheres) is needed: Hilton's theorem does not apply to wedges of circles (n = 2).

items.name: Rational homotopy of simply connected spheres
items.statement: For m≥2, π_i(S^m)⊗Q has rank 1 at i=m, and also at i=2m−1 if m is even, and is zero otherwise. Do not extend the statement blindly to S1 and nonconnected iterated loops.
items.locator: §7, proof of Lemma 7.6, p. 944 (arXiv v3: p. 46)
items.note: Review note: missing (Serre). The statement also holds for m = 1, but the restriction to m ≥ 2 is harmless.

items.name: Rational homotopy ranks in signed Euler notation
items.statement: For n≥3 and X≃∨_N S^{n−1}, dim_Q π_{r(n−2)+1}(X)⊗Q=(−1)^{r(n−2)−1}e_r(N); all other positive rational homotopy groups vanish. For odd n, include the second rational homotopy class of even spheres in the Möbius calculation.
items.locator: §7, proof of Lemma 7.6, pp. 944–945 (arXiv v3: pp. 46–47)
items.note: Review note: missing. The printed Möbius manipulations for n odd were checked for k = 2, 4, 6: M(N,k) + 1_{k≡2 (4)}M(N,k/2) = (1/k)Σ_{d|k}μ(d)(−N)^{k/d}. The item's range n ≥ 3 is correct.

items.name: Rational cohomology of the connected double-loop H-space
items.statement: For n≥4 and X≃∨_N S^{n−1}, Ω²X is connected and of finite rational type degreewise. Its rational cohomology is a free graded-commutative algebra on the dual rational homotopy generators shifted down two degrees, with ranks given by wedgehomotopy. Verify Sullivan p.311's hypotheses before treating this as closed.
items.locator: §7, proof of Lemma 7.6, p. 945 (arXiv v3: p. 47). Sullivan is [24, p. 311] in print but [25] in arXiv v3 (the reference list is reordered).
items.note: Review note: missing; debt G4. The restriction n ≥ 4 is exactly what is needed. Then π2(X)=0 makes ΩX simply connected, so Milnor–Moore applies to Ω²X = Ω(ΩX), and Samelson products vanish on a double loop space. The ranks are finite in each degree.

items.name: Double-loop Betti series in the connected range
items.statement: For n≥4 and smooth affine X⊂C^n with smooth degree-k leading form, dim H^j(Ω²X,Q)=[q^{−j}]∏_{r≥1}(1−(−q)^{1−r(n−2)})^{−e_r(N)}, where N=dim H^{n−1}(X,Q). This corrects the printed n≥2: at n=3 the full Ω²X can have infinitely many components. The coefficientwise product is well-defined for n≥4.
items.locator: §7, Lemma 7.6 and its proof, pp. 944–945 (arXiv v3: pp. 46–47)
items.note: Review note: REPAIR VERDICT: sound. The correction to n ≥ 4 is right (E4 confirmed). At n = 3 the k = 1 factor is (1−(−q)^0)^{−N}, which is undefined, and π0(Ω²X) = π2(X) = Z^N. The item and E4 miss n = 2, which also fails. There every factor has exponent 1−k(n−2) = 1, and infinitely many e_k(N) are nonzero once N ≥ 2, so the product is undefined too; Hilton's theorem does not apply there either. For n ≥ 4 the reviewer checked the formula by machine against the Poincaré series of the free graded-commutative algebra, for n=4..7, N ∈ {1,2,3,8} and j ≤ 25.

items.name: Conditional implication from the comparison conjecture
items.statement: Let K = C, d ≥ k−1 ≥ 2 and n > 2^k(k−1), and put D = d(n−k), t = ⌊d/(k−1)⌋ and δ = n/2^k − k + 1. Give Hom_{d,P}(C,X) a topology in which the analytic map from Mor_{d,P}(A^1,X)(C) is continuous and Hom_{d,P}(C,X) ≃ Ω²X (Lemma 7.2; stronggermgate), and assume Conjecture 7.1 for that topology. Take −4(tδ−1) < i ≤ 0. Then dim H_c^{i+2D}(Mor,Q) = dim H^{−i}(Ω²X,Q). This in turn equals Σ_{m=0}^{d} dim(H_c^{i+m(n−1)}(PConf_m,Q_ℓ) ⊗ H_c^{n−1}(X,Q_ℓ)^{⊗m} ⊗ sgn^{n−1})^{S_m}, by Lemma 7.6 (n ≥ 4), Corollary 7.5 (with j = −i < 4(tδ−1) ≤ d(n−3)) and the étale–singular comparison. This gives the isomorphism of Conjecture 1.3 in these degrees. For i > 0, Conjecture 1.3 says H_c^{i+2D}(Mor) = 0. This is (1.2)/cohsupport and needs Theorem 1.1's comparison at i: it holds in the conservative range i > −4(tδ−(k−1)) and is gated by comparisonsharpgate beyond it. In every degree where the comparison of Theorem 1.1 holds, the dimension equality forces every differential into or out of total degree i to vanish, so the spectral sequence degenerates at E1 there.
items.locator: §7, the argument before Theorem 7.7 and Theorem 7.7, pp. 945–946 (arXiv v3: pp. 47–48)
items.note: Review (REV-PAPER-BROWNING-SAWIN-20): statement corrected against the paper: 'The main parameter range' needs spelling out: K = C, d ≥ k−1 ≥ 2 and n > 2^k(k−1), the hypotheses of Conjecture 1.3. Conjecture 7.1 and Lemma 7.2 must be read for one and the same topology on Hom_{d,P}(C,X). The item makes the whole implication conditional on the sharp comparison. That is needed only for i > 0 (the vanishing (1.2)) and for the reading of Conjecture 1.3 as E1-degeneration. For −4(tδ−1) < i ≤ 0 the displayed isomorphism follows without Theorem 1.1. Review note: REPAIR VERDICT: sound. Adding provisos only weakens the statement, so the item is true. Two of its conditions are necessary: the mapping-space equivalence (E28) and H_c in place of H (E8). The sharp-comparison proviso is stronger than needed for i ≤ 0 (see statement_issue). The rational-homotopy prerequisites are source debts (G4), not doubts. dependsOn should include cohsupport for the i > 0 part.

items.name: Smooth trace and duality
items.statement: For smooth pure r-dimensional Y over a separably closed field, RΓ_c(Y,E)⊗RΓ(Y,E)→E[−2r](−r) is the Poincaré pairing. For geometrically connected Y, H_c^{2r}=E(−r). Retain the negative Tate twist.

items.name: Fourier input for the one-modulus trace map
items.statement: For a nonconstant one-variable polynomial f of degree <p, the exponential family on G_m has the cohomological support used in Lem.3.7: RΓ_c(G_m×A1,L_ψ(hf(a))) is concentrated in degrees ≤2. The cited Fourier middle-extension/no-constant-quotient argument must be checked against Katz §8.2.5(2), with all exclusions explicit.
items.locator: §3, proof of Lemma 3.7, pp.917–918, citing [15, 8.2.5(2)] ([16] in arXiv v3) (arXiv v3: p.23)
items.note: Review note: The statement is true, and the original-source gap can be closed with Fourier inversion alone, without Katz 8.2.5(2). Let D = deg f, with 1 ≤ D < p and E of characteristic 0. For h ≠ 0, RΓ_c(A^1_a, L_ψ(hf(a))) sits in degree 1, so the total complex is RΓ_c(G_m, G[−1]) with G = R^1pr_{h!}, and its only possible degree above 2 is H^3 = H^2_c(G_m, G). Split f_*E = E ⊕ F0 by the trace. F0 has no geometric invariants or coinvariants, because the cover f is connected and has finite monodromy. Put P = FT(F0[1]); then P|_{G_m} = G[1]. Inversion gives RΓ_c(A^1, P) = FT(P)_0[−1] = (F0)_0(−1), concentrated in degree 0, and P_0 = RΓ_c(A^1, F0)[2] is concentrated in degree −1, since H^2_c(A^1, F0) consists of coinvariants and vanishes. The triangle RΓ_c(G_m, G[1]) → RΓ_c(A^1, P) → P_0 then forces H^2_c(G_m, G) = 0. So this item depends only on fourierdeligne (inversion). It also agrees with the excision count dim H^2 = #roots − 1.

For arbitrary constructible compact supports use the 2r upper bound, not the affine r bound.

This is one explicit interpretation of the source, not a claim about an unstated intended topology.

items.name: Shrinking degree-one phase loop
items.statement: For 0<r≤1/4 and s∈[0,1], put h(s,r)=max(0,min(1,(s−r)/r)) and σ(s,r)=exp(2πi h(s,r)). Descend in s through 0∼1. The lift h is retained for the integer monodromy computation.

items.statement: For the Fermat pair let r(T)=1/(4(1+|T|)), a_s(T)=T^d σ(s,r(T)), and F_s(T)=(a_s(T),ζa_s(T),1,0,…), extended at∞ by P. This is a based continuous loop S1→Hco at g. items.name: A compact parameter family has a common projective chart at infinity
items.statement: For compact K and continuous H:K→Hco, there is R0 such that H(u,T) lies in {x1≠0} for all u∈K and |T|>R0, assuming P has x1≠0. Joint evaluation and a finite subcover of K×{∞} give a common neighbourhood of∞. The normal coordinate v=x0/x1 is nonzero there for finite T because H(u,T)∈X. This does not assert uniform convergence of v/z^d.

The tube lemma then gives a common R0. Finite points map into X, so x0 ≠ 0 and v = x0/x1 ∈ C*. The item rightly makes no claim about v/z^d.

items.name: Winding of a mapping-space loop at infinity
items.statement: For a based loop γ:S1→Hco in the Fermat example, choose any sufficiently large positive R and take the degree of the circle-valued normalization of γ(s)(R).x0/γ(s)(R).x1, divided by its value at the loop basepoint. This defines endWind:π1(Hco,g)→Z after proving the independence and homotopy relations below.

items.name: End winding is independent of radius and based homotopy
items.statement: For two admissible radii use the radial interval between them and compactchart. For a based homotopy use compactchart with K=I×S1. All normal coordinates remain in C*, so their normalized phases form a homotopy of loops. A common radius for two loops proves additivity by the circle fundamental-group isomorphism.
