A based homotopy I × S^1 → Hco gets a common R0 from compactchart with K = I × S^1. For a concatenation, take the larger of the two radii; the degrees add.

items.name: Infinite-order loop in the compact-open germ space
items.statement: In the Fermat example, endWind([F])=−1; hence endWind is surjective and [F] has infinite order. In particular F does not bound a disk in Hco. A hypothetical disk gives by compactchart a disk in C* with boundary R^(−d)σ(s,r(R))^(−1), whose degree is−1.
items.locator: extraction's own construction, not in the paper; it concerns §7, (7.1) and Lemma 7.2 with its proof, pp. 940–941 (arXiv v3: pp. 43–44)
items.note: Review note: REPAIR VERDICT: sound. A filling H: D² → Hco would, by compactchart with K = D², give a map D² → C* whose boundary loop has degree −1. That is impossible. Since endWind is a homomorphism with endWind([F]) = −1, it is surjective, and [F] has infinite order.

items.name: Join of finite nonempty sets has the required connectivity
items.statement: For n≥2 finite nonempty discrete sets A_j of sizes k_j, their join has the homotopy type of a wedge of ∏(k_j−1) spheres S^(n−1), with a zero product meaning a point. Inductively join a CW complex Y with k points, collapse one contractible cone, and obtain k−1 copies of the reduced suspension of Y. Cellular approximation gives (n−2)-connectivity. Generic CW/cofibration and cellular approximation are imported, not replaced by a list of homology ranks.
items.locator: extraction's own lemma, not in the paper; used for the E28 comparison target
acceptance: If one factor is a singleton the join is contractible.
items.note: Review note: REPAIR VERDICT: sound. Y ∗ (k points) is k cones on Y glued along Y. Collapsing one contractible cone leaves the wedge of k−1 copies of CY/Y ≅ SY. Starting from k_1 points = ∨_{k_1−1} S^0, induction gives ∨_{∏(k_j−1)} S^{n−1}, and a factor with k_j = 1 gives a cone. The acceptance tests are correct.

items.name: Fermat fibre comparison with a finite join
items.statement: For f=Σ_{j=1}^n z_j^k, k≥2, the positive-phase fibre f^−1(R_{>0}) retracts onto the join of n copies of μ_k (Milnor, Lemma9.2). The explicit homeomorphism u↦(f(u)^(−1/k)u,f(u)) identifies it with X×R_{>0}. Thus X is homotopy equivalent to that join; this special homogeneous case does not discharge the general tame-fibre theorem.
items.locator: Milnor, Singular Points of Complex Hypersurfaces (1968), §9 (Pham's join lemma), pp. 73–74. Not in the paper; used for the E28 comparison target at §7, Lemma 7.2, pp. 940–941 (arXiv v3: pp. 43–44).
items.note: Review note: REPAIR VERDICT: sound. u ↦ (f(u)^{−1/k}u, f(u)) is a homeomorphism f^{-1}(R_{>0}) ≅ X × R_{>0} with inverse (x,t) ↦ t^{1/k}x, by homogeneity. That X is homotopy equivalent to the join of n copies of μ_k is Pham's classical theorem (1965), reproduced in Milnor §9. The reviewer did not re-read the lemma number in Milnor, but the mathematics does not depend on it. The statement rightly does not claim the general Broughton theorem.

items.name: Vanishing of the comparison double-loop fundamental group
items.statement: For the Fermat X and n≥5, finitejoin and fermatjoin give π2(X)=π3(X)=0. Hence Ω²X is path connected and π1(Ω²X)=0, using the pinned loop-space shift at m=0,n=2 and its components equivalence.
items.locator: extraction's own deduction, not in the paper; used for the E28 comparison target
items.note: Review note: REPAIR VERDICT: sound. For n ≥ 5, X ≃ ∨ S^{n−1} is 3-connected, so π0(Ω²X) = π2(X) = 0 (zerothHomotopyEquiv) and π1(Ω²X, const) = π3(X) = 0 (piLoopSpaceMulEquiv 0 2). Path-connectedness then gives π1 = 0 at every basepoint. For n = 40 the space Ω²X is in fact 36-connected.

items.name: Compact-open interpretation of Lemma7.2 fails in the main range
items.statement: For k=3,d=2,n=40, the nonempty compact-open prescribed-germ space Hco has a fundamental group surjecting onto Z, whereas Ω²X is path connected and simply connected. Consequently Hco is not homotopy equivalent to Ω²X. This refutes the compact-open interpretation, not every topology that could be intended in the unstated source convention.
items.locator: extraction's own construction, not in the paper; it concerns §7, (7.1) and Lemma 7.2 with its proof, pp. 940–941 (arXiv v3: pp. 43–44)
items.note: Review note: REPAIR VERDICT: sound; this establishes E28 for the compact-open reading. Any homotopy equivalence Hco → Ω²X would induce an isomorphism π1(Hco,g) ≅ π1(Ω²X,·) = 0, but π1(Hco,g) surjects onto Z. The obstruction survives rationally, since H^1(Hco;Q) ≠ 0 = H^1(Ω²X;Q). So the step of Theorem 7.7 that uses Lemma 7.2, H^{−i}(Hom,Q) = H^{−i}(Ω²X,Q), also fails for Hco. The counterexample lies in the paper's main range (d = k−1 = 2, n > 2^k(k−1)).

items.name: A chart with uniform control of the normalized germ
items.statement: Fix a product chart (u,v) near P in Xbar with divisor v=0, a radius ε>0, and a convex tangential ball. For 0<|z|≤ε require u(z)=O(|z|), w(z)=v(z)/z^d=1+O(|z|), u in that ball, and |w−1|<1/2. Equip such tails with the weighted supremum distances of u/|z| and (w−1)/|z|, and combine with the compact-open topology away from the tail. The model includes the fixed radius as data; it is not yet an all-germs topology.

items.name: Fixed-collar extension-space comparison contract
items.statement: For a fixed boundary loop β:S1→X with β(b)=x and a chosen extension to D², let Ext(β) be the compact-open space of extensions. The restriction Map_*(D²,X)→Map_*(S1,X) has the homotopy-lifting property by the CW boundary cofibration and compact-open adjunction; its total space contracts by a disk contraction fixing b. Thus its fibre over β is homotopy equivalent to Ω²X after choosing the reference nullhomotopy. This is a fixed-collar supplier, not an equivalence for Hco.
items.locator: extraction's own construction, not in the paper; it concerns §7, (7.1) and Lemma 7.2 with its proof, pp. 940–941 (arXiv v3: pp. 43–44)

items.note: Review note: REPAIR VERDICT: sound. S^1 → D² is a based cofibration, so the based restriction Map_*(D²,X) → Map_*(S^1,X) is a Hurewicz fibration (exponential law for compact Hausdorff D²). Its total space contracts by (x,t) ↦ (1−t)x + tb, which fixes b. The fibre over β is nonempty exactly when β is null-homotopic, and then it is homotopy equivalent to the fibre over the constant loop, which is Ω²X. The item correctly treats the reference extension as a hypothesis.

items.name: Unclosed stronger-germ comparison
items.statement: To recover the source endpoint choose a topology controlling normalized germs uniformly in compact parameter families, prove continuity of the polynomial-map inclusion, and compare its mapping space with fixedcollarloops using collarstraightening. No such global comparison is proved here. If it has the claimed Ω²X homotopy type, its inclusion into Hco cannot be a weak equivalence in the Fermat example.

items.note: Review note: REPAIR VERDICT: sound as an honestly labelled open gate. Its one assertion is correct: a model with the homotopy type of Ω²X cannot include into Hco by a weak equivalence in the Fermat example. One concrete candidate topology is the colimit over (ε,C) of the closed subspaces {|u| ≤ C|z|, |w−1| ≤ C|z| on |z| ≤ ε}, each with the compact-open topology. Compact families then lie in a single stage, and collarstraightening applies there once Cε < 1/2. The polynomial inclusion is continuous because the O-constants are locally bounded on Mor(C). This is a suggestion, not a proof.

items.name: Smooth projective closure of X and its irreducibility
items.statement: Let K be a field with char K = 0 or char K > k, n ≥ 2, and f ∈ K[x1,…,xn] of degree k whose degree-k part f0 defines a smooth hypersurface Z ⊂ P^{n−1} and whose zero set X ⊂ A^n is smooth. Then the homogenization F(x0,…,xn) = x0^k f(x/x0) defines a smooth hypersurface X̄ ⊂ P^n with X̄ ∩ {x0 = 0} = Z scheme-theoretically and X = X̄ \ Z. Consequently X̄ is geometrically connected, hence geometrically irreducible, of dimension n−1; X is a non-empty dense open subset, hence geometrically irreducible; and the trace H_c^{2(n−1)}(X_K̄, E) → E(−(n−1)) is an isomorphism.
items.locator: §3, Lemma 3.7 (hypothesis) p.917, proof of Lemma 3.11 pp.919–920; §4, Lemma 4.2 pp.922–923 (arXiv v3: pp.23, 25–26, 27–28)

The paper assumes the first ('X irreducible') and asserts the second ('X̄ and D are both smooth projective hypersurfaces') without proof. Route: GeometricCircleMethodAndMappingSpaces.

items.name: Hyperplane-class description of hypersurface cohomology
items.statement: Let Y ⊂ P^{N+1} be a smooth hypersurface of degree k over a separably closed field of characteristic ≠ ℓ, and η = c1(O(1)). For 0 ≤ i ≤ 2N with i ≠ N: H^i(Y, E) = E·η^{i/2} ≅ E(−i/2) if i is even and 0 if i is odd. If D = Y ∩ H is a smooth hyperplane section, restriction sends η^j to η^j, so H^i(Y) → H^i(D) is an isomorphism for N < i ≤ 2N−2 and surjective for i = N. The primitive middle cohomology has rank ((k−1)^{N+2} + (−1)^N (k−1))/k; for N even this is (1−1/k)((k−1)^{N+1} + 1), the N1 of Lemma 4.3.
items.locator: §3, proof of Lemma 3.11, p.920; §4, proofs of Lemmas 4.2 and 4.3, pp.923–924 (arXiv v3: p.26; pp.27–29)

items.name: Compact-support cohomology of a finite étale Galois quotient
items.statement: Let π: Y → Y' be a finite étale Galois cover with group G of separated schemes of finite type over a separably closed field, E a field of characteristic 0, and F ∈ D^b_c(Y', E). Then G acts on RΓ_c(Y, π^*F), and the trace map π_*π^*F → F induces an isomorphism RΓ_c(Y', F) ≅ RΓ_c(Y, π^*F)^G; taking G-invariants is exact because |G| is invertible in E.
items.locator: §3, proof of Lemma 3.9, p.919; Figure 2, p.921 (arXiv v3: pp.24, 26)

items.name: Top compact cohomology and top-dimensional components
items.statement: Let M be a separated scheme of finite type and dimension m over an algebraically closed field. Then H^i_c(M, E) = 0 for i > 2m, and H^{2m}_c(M, E) ≅ E(−m)^{c}, where c is the number of m-dimensional irreducible components of M. Proof: excise a closed Z of dimension ≤ m−1 so that U = M_red \ Z is smooth of pure dimension m, with one connected component per top-dimensional component, and use Poincaré duality on U. Hence if every irreducible component of M has dimension ≥ D, H^i_c(M) = 0 for i > 2D and dim H^{2D}_c(M) = 1, then M is irreducible of dimension D.
items.locator: §2, proof of Corollary 2.9, pp.907–908 (arXiv v3: p.14)

items.name: Geometric monodromy group of a lisse sheaf
items.statement: For a lisse E-sheaf F on a connected normal scheme S of finite type over a field k and a geometric point ξ̄, G_geom(F) is the Zariski closure in GL(F_ξ̄) of the image of π1(S_k̄, ξ̄); it is independent of ξ̄ up to conjugacy. Morphisms of lisse sheaves, and so their kernels, cokernels and subquotients, are G_geom-equivariant. If 0 → F' → F → F'' → 0 is exact, G_geom(F) surjects onto G_geom(F' ⊕ F''), which projects onto G_geom(F') and G_geom(F''). If g: T → S is a morphism of connected normal schemes inducing a surjection π1(T_k̄) → π1(S_k̄), then G_geom(g^*F) = G_geom(F).
items.locator: §4, after Lemma 4.3, pp.923–924, and proof of Lemma 4.3, p.924 (arXiv v3: pp.28–29)
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-BROWNING-SAWIN-20 (coverage of the paper): Items universalmonodromy, algebraicgoursat, minusone and oddpages use it, and none defines it. Route: UniversalHypersurfaceMonodromy.

items.name: Relative major-arc spectral sequence over the universal pair
items.statement: Let e_M: M_{n,k} × A^{dn} × A^{kd} → A^1 be the universal phase and S^M = R p_! e_M^*L_ψ on M_{n,k} × A^{kd}. By proper base change its restriction to a geometric point (f, x) is S_{d,f}. The open filtration M_{n,k} × (A_d^{kd} \ A_{m−1}^{kd}), 0 ≤ m ≤ d+1, gives a convergent spectral sequence of constructible sheaves on M_{n,k}, with E1^{m,s} = R^{m+s}pr_{M,m!}S^M ⇒ R^{m+s}p̄r_{M,d!}S^M, whose stalk at every geometric point is the spectral sequence of Proposition 2.5 for that (f, x). M_{n,k} is irreducible. When every E1 term is lisse (Lemma 4.4), every page consists of lisse sheaves and every differential is equivariant for π1(M_{n,k,F̄_q}), hence for the geometric monodromy group.
items.locator: §4, p.922 (relative S_{d,f}, pr_{M,m}) and proof of Proposition 4.1, pp.926–927 (arXiv v3: pp.26–27; pp.30–31)
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-BROWNING-SAWIN-20 (coverage of the paper): Proposition 4.1 needs this spectral sequence of lisse sheaves on M_{n,k}, whose stalks are the spectral sequence of Proposition 2.5. Item finitefiltration covers only one base Y, and item relativestratum only its E1 terms. Route: GeometricCircleMethodAndMappingSpaces.

items.name: Fibre-dimension stratification
items.statement: Let φ: V → Y be a morphism of schemes of finite type over a field. The function y ↦ dim φ^{−1}(y), with value −∞ on empty fibres, is constructible on Y. Hence Y has a finite partition into locally closed irreducible subsets W_j on each of which the function takes a constant value e_j. When e_j ≥ 0, dim φ^{−1}(W_j) = e_j + dim W_j, and in particular e_j ≤ dim V − dim W_j.

items.name: Closed points detect constructible supports over a finite field
items.statement: Let X be a scheme of finite type over F_q and K a bounded constructible ℓ-adic complex on X. Suppose that for every r ≥ 1 and every x ∈ X(F_{q^r}), the stalk of H^i(K) at a geometric point over x vanishes. Then H^i(K) = 0. Equivalently, the support of H^i(K) is a constructible subset of X, and a constructible subset of X that contains no closed point is empty.
items.locator: §5, proof of Proposition 5.8, p. 934, and the proof of Proposition 5.5, p. 931 (arXiv v3: pp. 34, 37)
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-BROWNING-SAWIN-20 (coverage of the paper): The last step of Prop. 5.8 and the stalkwise bound on Rπ_! in Prop. 5.5 both deduce vanishing of a constructible sheaf from its vanishing at F_{q^r}-points. No item states this. The topological half is in Mathlib: Topology.IsConstructible (Mathlib/Topology/Constructible.lean:178), nonempty_inter_closedPoints (Mathlib/Topology/JacobsonSpace.lean:107) and LocallyOfFiniteType.jacobsonSpace (Mathlib/AlgebraicGeometry/Morphisms/FiniteType.lean:113). The sheaf half, that the support of a constructible sheaf is constructible, belongs with constructible sheaves. Route: GeometricCircleMethodAndMappingSpaces.

items.name: Affine dimension theorem for intersections
items.statement: Let F be an algebraically closed field and let Y, Z ⊂ A^M_F be irreducible closed subvarieties with Y ∩ Z ≠ ∅. Every irreducible component of Y ∩ Z has dimension ≥ dim Y + dim Z − M. Consequence: if V ⊂ A^M_F is closed, every irreducible component of V meets an irreducible Z (for instance, V is stable under scaling and 0 ∈ Z), and dim(V ∩ Z) ≤ 0, then dim V ≤ M − dim Z.
items.locator: §6, proof of Proposition 6.2, p. 939 (the paper cites no source; Hartshorne, Prop. I.7.1) (arXiv v3: p. 43)

It is not planned in the atlas. Mathlib has Krull's height theorem (Ideal.height_le_spanRank, Mathlib/RingTheory/Ideal/KrullsHeightTheorem.lean:266) as an ingredient. The componentwise lower bound in dimensionlower (item 2) rests on the same Krull-type input and should share its owner. Route: GeometricCircleMethodAndMappingSpaces.

items.name: Analytic polynomial-map inclusion into the germ mapping space
items.statement: For g = (g_1,…,g_n) ∈ Mor_{d,P}(A^1,X)(C), with g_j = x_jT^d + lower terms, put ι(g)(T) = [g_1(T):…:g_n(T):1] for T ∈ C and ι(g)(∞) = P. In the coordinate z = T^{−1} this is [x_1+O(|z|):…:x_n+O(|z|):z^d], so ι(g) satisfies (7.1). The map (g,T) ↦ ι(g)(T) is jointly continuous on Mor(C)^an × P^1(C), because the leading coefficients are fixed and the O-constants are locally bounded in the coefficients. Hence ι: Mor(C)^an → Hco is continuous for the compact-open topology, and also for any colimit-of-controlled-germs topology in which the O-constants are locally uniform.
items.locator: §7, sentence after (7.1), p. 940 (arXiv v3: p. 43)
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-BROWNING-SAWIN-20 (coverage of the paper): Conjecture 7.1 (functoriality) and Theorem 7.7 use this map, and stronggermgate needs its continuity. It appears only as an API line in localgerm. Route: GeometricCircleMethodAndMappingSpaces.

items.name: Euler products for squarefree and all monic polynomials over F_q
items.statement: In Z[[U]], with g running over the monic irreducible polynomials in F_q[t]: (1) Σ_{f monic} U^{deg f} = (1−qU)^{−1} = ∏_g (1−U^{deg g})^{−1}; (2) for every integer a, Σ_{f monic squarefree} a^{ω(f)}U^{deg f} = ∏_g(1+aU^{deg g}); (3) hence, if ∏_{k≥1}(1−T^k)^{−e_k} = 1+aT, then Σ_{f squarefree} a^{ω(f)}U^{deg f} = ∏_{k≥1}(1−qU^k)^{−e_k}.
items.locator: §7, proof of Lemma 7.4, p. 943 (arXiv v3: p. 45)
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-BROWNING-SAWIN-20 (coverage of the paper): Lemma 7.4 uses Σ_{f squarefree} a^{ω(f)}U^{deg f} = ∏_g(1+aU^{deg g}) and ζ_{F_q[t]}(s) = (1−q^{1−s})^{−1}. Neither Mathlib (no count of monic irreducibles at 082e2d3) nor any atlas stage has them. Route: ConfigurationSpacesAndRationalLoops.

items.name: Invariant dimensions via characters for S_m-twisted tensor powers
items.statement: Let E be a field of characteristic 0, W a finite-dimensional E[S_m]-module and V an N-dimensional E-vector space with S_m permuting the tensor factors of V^{⊗m}. Then dim(W ⊗ V^{⊗m} ⊗ sgn^{n−1})^{S_m} = (1/m!) Σ_σ χ_W(σ) N^{c(σ)} ((−1)^{m−c(σ)})^{n−1}, where c(σ) is the number of cycles of σ, fixed points included.
items.locator: §7, proof of Lemma 7.4, p. 942 (arXiv v3: pp. 44–45)
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-BROWNING-SAWIN-20 (coverage of the paper): The proof uses dim W^{S_m} = ⟨χ_W,1⟩, χ_{V^{⊗m}}(σ) = N^{c(σ)} and sgn(σ) = (−1)^{m−c(σ)}. Mathlib has the first and the last. The permutation-character count is elementary but should be an item with library credit. Status: missing rather than library; the formula is a short computation from mathlib:FDRep.average_char_eq_finrank_invariants, mathlib:Equiv.Perm.sign_of_cycleType (both exist at Mathlib 082e2d3), not itself in the library. items.name: Conjecture 7.1 fails for the compact-open germ space in the Fermat example
items.statement: Take X = {x_1^3+…+x_40^3 = 1} ⊂ C^40, P = [1:ζ:0:…:0] with ζ^3 = −1, d = 2, D = 74, and Hom = Hco with the subspace compact-open topology. Then H^1(Hco;Q) ≠ 0, because endWind: π1(Hco,g) ↠ Z factors through H_1. But H_c^{2D−1}(Mor_{2,P}(A^1,X),Q) = 0 by cohsupport at i = −1, which lies in the conservative range i > −4. So the pairing of Conjecture 7.1 at j = 1 (0 ≤ 1 < 8) is not perfect.
items.locator: §7, Conjecture 7.1 and (7.1), p. 940 (arXiv v3: p. 43); reviewer's addition
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-BROWNING-SAWIN-20 (coverage of the paper): This shows that the intended topology on Hom_{d,P}(C,X) must be finer than compact-open, so the conjecture itself, not only Lemma 7.2, depends on it. It uses only checked items: windingnonzero and cohsupport. Route: GeometricCircleMethodAndMappingSpaces.

review.reason: Take (k,d,n) = (3,4,24), so δ = 1, t = 2, and the claimed cutoff is 2dn + 4 − 4tδ = 188. The stratum m = 5 (≤ m_0 = 5) has B(5) = 24(8 − 1) + 24 = 192 > 188. More generally B(d) = [2dn + 4 − 4tδ] + 4(d − (k−1)t), which already exceeds the claim when k−1 does not divide d. When k−1 divides d, the stratum m = d+1 exceeds it by 4, and m = d+1 ≤ m_0 unless (k,d) = (3,2). So the printed proof establishes Prop. 2.6 exactly when (k,d) = (3,2), where the only stratum is m = d = 2. This refutes the inference, not the proposition; the paper gives no other route. It affects Prop. 2.6 and the ranges in Thm. 1.1, Thm. 2.7(3), Cor. 1.2, Conj. 1.3 and Cor. 1.4 ((1.1)). review.reason: Verified in print. With t·δ = 1, Theorem 1.1/2.7(3) identifies the limit complex with H^{i+2d(n−k)}_c only for i > 0. At i = 0, excision gives only H^{2nd}_c(A^{kd}) → H^{2nd}_c(A_d) surjective, because H^{2nd+1}_c(A^{kd} \ A_d) = 0 while H^{2nd}_c(A^{kd} \ A_d) need not vanish. So dim H^{2d(n−k)}_c(M) ≥ dim E∞^{0,0} = 1: an upper bound of 1, needed for a unique top component, is not available. The i > 0 part is fine at equality, since the range is then exactly i > 0. The tδ > k−1 clause rests on E2 (§5, p.934, outside this range); I checked its arithmetic, B(m) = 2dn − 4⌊m/(k−1)⌋δ + 4(r+1) with r = m mod (k−1), which gives the stated bound. There the sharp range is actually proved, because (k,d) = (3,2) is the one case where the printed proof of Prop. 2.6 is complete (E2). So this is a failure of the Cor. 1.4 argument in its own right, independent of E2.
